model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos, NeuN (RBFOX3), DAPI]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires mapping behaviorally activated neurons across the entire adult mouse brain at single-cell resolution. c-Fos is a canonical immediate-early gene marker for neuronal activation and must be immunolabeled due to lack of endogenous fluorescence. NeuN provides pan-neuronal nuclear labeling to contextualize c-Fos+ cells within the total neuronal population, while DAPI offers general nuclear counterstaining for anatomical registration. iDISCO+ is selected because it enables whole-brain immunolabeling with excellent antibody penetration, strong autofluorescence quenching, high transparency, and compatibility with standard fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor conjugates). Its organic solvent-based protocol preserves protein epitopes better than some aqueous methods for c-Fos and supports long-term sample stability—critical for large-volume imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching and Lipid Peroxidation  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum: anti-c-Fos (rabbit, 1:500), anti-NeuN (mouse, 1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Washes Post Primary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor dyes (e.g., anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 for c-Fos, anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 for NeuN; 1:500) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

8 Washes Post Secondary Antibody  
8.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (Post-Immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Nuclear Counterstaining (Optional but recommended for registration)  
12.1 Prior to final DBE step, rehydrate briefly through methanol series to 80% methanol, then incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
12.2 Re-dehydrate through methanol series (80% → 100%) and repeat steps 10.1–11.2.  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Mount cleared brain in glass-bottom dish or custom chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos + Alexa Fluor 488, Npas4 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole adult mouse brains due to its strong delipidation capability, compatibility with endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, and excellent preservation of nuclear and cytoplasmic immediate early gene (IEG) signals like c-Fos and Npas4. It enables high-resolution 3D mapping of activated neuronal ensembles across the entire brain. The use of two distinct IEG markers (c-Fos and Npas4) labeled with spectrally separable Alexa Fluor dyes allows discrimination of functionally distinct neuronal subpopulations activated by specific behavioral paradigms. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for registration and cell segmentation. iDISCO+’s organic solvent–based refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.56) is compatible with light-sheet microscopy and preserves Alexa Fluor signal intensity better than many aqueous methods.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  
1.3 Store in PBST at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

3 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching and Permeabilization  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.3 Wash in PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

4 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation in blocking buffer: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: rabbit anti-c-Fos (1:500) and goat anti-Npas4 (1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 3% normal donkey serum + 0.2% heparin + 1% DMSO) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

5 Washing After Primary Antibody  
5.1 Wash in PBST + 0.2% heparin (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours × 3 changes, total 3 days)  

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500) + DAPI (1:1000) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

7 Washing After Secondary Antibody  
7.1 Wash in PBST + 0.2% heparin (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours × 3 changes, total 3 days, protected from light)  

8 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

9 Delipidation  
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes × 2 changes)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer cleared brain into a glass imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE and mount for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) within 24 hours (store at RT, protected from light if not imaged immediately)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos, Npas4, Alexa Fluor 488 / Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** The original CUBIC protocol failed due to insufficient delipidation and poor penetration in dense adult mouse brain tissue. iDISCO+ is superior for whole adult mouse brains because it combines effective methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM)-based delipidation, enabling deep, homogeneous clearing while preserving endogenous fluorescence and allowing robust immunolabeling of nuclear immediate early gene (IEG) products like c-Fos and Npas4. These two IEGs define distinct activated neuron subpopulations with different temporal dynamics and functional roles. Using directly conjugated Alexa Fluor secondary antibodies ensures high signal-to-noise, compatibility with iDISCO+ organic solvents, and minimal cross-talk for dual-channel imaging at single-cell resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-c-Fos (e.g., Santa Cruz sc-52, 1:500) and anti-Npas4 (e.g., Cell Signaling #14299, 1:250) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washes after Primary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), both diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Washes after Secondary Antibody  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 changes)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer brain to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; image within 1 week for optimal fluorescence)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for fixed, lipid-rich neural tissues like spinal cord, offering excellent delipidation and deep clearing of ~15 mm samples while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence. It enables long-range axonal tracing in 3D with high signal-to-background. The dual labeling strategy targets regenerating/immature axons (β-III Tubulin/TUJ1) and mature/ensheathed axons (MBP), allowing spatial discrimination between regenerative fibers and preserved myelinated tracts around the lesion core. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are highly compatible with iDISCO+ due to their photostability and resistance to organic solvents.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-MBP (1:250) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:500) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Repeat step 10.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared sample in DBE at RT, protected from light, for up to 2 weeks prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: as needed)

It effectively clears lipid-rich neural tissue while retaining endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence over millimeter-scale samples. The chosen labeling targets β-III Tubulin (a pan-neuronal/axonal marker) for long-range axon tracing, GFAP to delineate reactive astrocytic borders around the lesion core, and DAPI for nuclear reference—all compatible with CUBIC’s high-pH reagents and suitable for deep 3D imaging without requiring transgenic reporters. Avoiding electrophoresis eliminates mechanical stress that caused tissue fragmentation in prior attempts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) PVP, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (1:500), anti-GFAP (1:500) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (10% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times, changing solution daily (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (or mCherry) for specific cortical projection neurons, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)+Alexa Fluor 647 for pan-axonal background labeling]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, intact mouse CNS samples (up to 40 mm) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of red-shifted fluorescent proteins (e.g., tdTomato/mCherry), and compatibility with immunolabeling in thick tissues. The methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM)/dibenzyl ether (DBE) clearing enable deep penetration and high transparency across brain–spinal cord continuity. Dual labeling with a genetically encoded red fluorophore (tdTomato) in projection neurons and an anti–β-III Tubulin antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 allows simultaneous visualization of specific long-range projections against the full axonal scaffold, enabling precise discrimination of target pathways from endogenous fiber tracts during 3D reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for immunolabeling)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody: anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted 1:500 in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Washes after Primary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, diluted 1:300 in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

8 Washes after Secondary Antibody  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunolabeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥12 hours)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE. Seal to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent lipid removal, high transparency, and strong preservation of antibody-based fluorescence—critical for detecting sparse amyloid-β deposits in 5XFAD brains. It is compatible with organic solvent–based refractive index matching (e.g., DBE), enabling high-resolution light-sheet imaging across the entire brain. The dual labeling strategy uses 6E10/4G8 antibodies (specific for human Aβ1–16 and Aβ17–24, respectively) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 for robust, far-red detection of amyloid plaques, combined with DAPI for nuclear counterstaining to enable accurate brain region registration and volumetric normalization. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly stable in iDISCO+’s methanol/detergent environment, and DAPI signal survives dehydration steps when added post-clearing or during rehydration.

5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)

10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 488, Congo red + TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount immunolabeling of fixed mouse brains, offering excellent lipid removal, strong autofluorescence quenching, and high compatibility with antibody-based detection of amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques. It preserves the structural integrity of dense Aβ deposits while enabling deep-tissue penetration of antibodies. The dual-labeling strategy uses 6E10/4G8 (pan-Aβ antibodies) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 for specific, high-sensitivity detection of Aβ conformers, and Congo red—a classic amyloidophilic dye that binds β-sheet-rich aggregates—with spectral properties distinct from Alexa Fluor 488, enabling orthogonal validation of plaque morphology and distribution. TO-PRO-3 provides nuclear counterstain compatible with iDISCO+’s organic solvents and far-red imaging window, facilitating regional annotation without spectral overlap.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Rehydration through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
2.3 Incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Blocking and Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBST + 5% DMSO + 0.2% Tween-20 + 0.3 M glycine).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody mix: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 5% DMSO + 0.2% Tween-20 + 0.01% NaN₃).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with PBST + 0.2% Tween-20 (6 changes over 2 days, 4–6 hours per wash).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: total 48 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-secondary Washes  
6.1 Wash with PBST + 0.2% Tween-20 (6 changes over 2 days).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: total 48 hours)  

7 Congo Red Staining  
7.1 Incubation with 0.05% (wt/vol) Congo red in 70% ethanol (filtered, pH adjusted to 8.0 with NaOH).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
7.2 Wash with 70% ethanol (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

8 Nuclear Counterstaining  
8.1 Incubation with 1 µM TO-PRO-3 in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
8.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

9 Dehydration (Post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

12.1 Transfer brain to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite for short-term; up to 1 month)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor 488, Congo red + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole adult mouse brains (~10 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, and compatibility with hydrophobic mounting media (e.g., DBE) that enable high-resolution light-sheet imaging. The dual-target labeling strategy combines two orthogonal amyloid-β (Aβ) detection methods: (1) monoclonal antibodies 6E10 (binds Aβ1–16) and 4G8 (binds Aβ17–24), conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 for high-specificity immunofluorescence; and (2) Congo red—a classic amyloidophilic dye—co-stained with Alexa Fluor 594 to provide a complementary, conformation-dependent signal. This dual validation minimizes false positives from autofluorescence or non-specific aggregates, enabling robust 3D quantification of plaque burden across brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Rehydration: sequential incubation with 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
2.3 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [6E10 / 4G8 + Alexa Fluor, Congo red]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol-based, organic solvent clearing method optimized for whole mouse brains, offering excellent lipid removal, deep tissue penetration, and superior preservation of antibody-based fluorescence—critical for detecting sparse, deep Aβ plaques in 5XFAD brains. The original protocol failed due to insufficient antigen accessibility and poor antibody penetration in fixed tissue; iDISCO+ includes permeabilization (Triton X-100) and delipidation steps that enhance antibody access to dense amyloid cores. Using both 6E10/4G8 (pan-Aβ antibodies conjugated to bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes) and Congo red (a classic amyloidophilic dye with intrinsic fluorescence upon binding β-sheet structures) provides orthogonal validation: antibodies offer high specificity and subcellular resolution, while Congo red labels all cross-β-sheet aggregates regardless of epitope masking, improving detection of compact/cored plaques in deep regions. Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with iDISCO+’s dehydration and organic solvents, retaining strong signal after DBE matching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Bleaching  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.6 Rehydration: sequential incubation with 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

2 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: 6E10 (1:500) and 4G8 (1:500), both diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine, 20% DMSO, 5% normal donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with PTwH (0.2% Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin in PBS), 3 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

4 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibodies (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488 or 647, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-immunostaining Washes  
5.1 Wash with PTwH, 3 changes over 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.2% Tween-20, 2 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

6 Congo Red Staining  
6.1 Incubation with 0.2% (wt/vol) Congo red in 50% ethanol (in distilled water), protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Wash with 50% ethanol, then 30% ethanol, then PBS + 0.2% Tween-20, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.2 Transfer to fresh 100% DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Store cleared brain in sealed DBE-filled glass vial at RT, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite for short-term; image within 1 week for optimal fluorescence)  
10.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, GFAP + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for fixed mouse brain tissue of this size (~8 mm scale), offering rapid, high-quality clearing with excellent preservation of protein epitopes and fluorescence signals when combined with robust Alexa Fluor dyes. It effectively removes lipids while maintaining 3D architecture of vasculature and tumor microenvironment. CD31 labels endothelial cells to visualize the entire vascular network (including fine branches and density), while GFAP highlights reactive astrocytes and glioma cell processes—critical for delineating tumor boundaries and assessing perivascular invasion by GBM cells. The methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane/DBE-based RI matching are compatible with Alexa Fluor conjugates and provide high transparency suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging of deep tumor-vascular interfaces.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for endogenous fluorescence reduction; skip if only exogenous labeling used)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 (1:200) and rabbit anti-GFAP (1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT (6 changes over 2 days).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT (6 changes over 2 days).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat 100% DCM incubation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE in glass vial for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

12 Storage / Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE at RT in the dark. Mount in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: as needed for imaging)

我尝试使用 CUBIC 处理 GBM 脑组织，但透明化后肿瘤组织形态破坏严重，血管网络出现断裂，导致无法可靠分析肿瘤边界、血管连续性和沿血管侵袭路径。原 protocol 为：CUBIC-L 在 37°C 处理 7 天，然后直接放入 CUBIC-R。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法，使其适合肿瘤脑组织形态保持、血管网络连续性保留、屏障相关结构检测和深层三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488, GFAP+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard-to-clear, lipid-rich tissues like brain tumors while preserving fine vascular architecture and protein epitopes. Unlike CUBIC—which causes excessive swelling and structural disintegration in glioblastoma due to strong chaotropic agents—PEGASOS uses a mild, polyethylene glycol–based delipidation and refractive index matching system that maintains tissue integrity, vascular continuity, and blood–brain barrier (BBB) protein structures (e.g., Claudin-5). The selected markers enable simultaneous visualization of endothelial cells (CD31), tight junctions of the BBB (Claudin-5), reactive astrocytes/tumor stroma (GFAP), and nuclei (DAPI), all critical for assessing tumor–vascular spatial relationships and barrier integrity across tumor core, margin, and parenchyma. Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with PEGASOS’ organic-aqueous hybrid chemistry and retain brightness after clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Delipidation Solution (5% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 70%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, 30 min each)  
3.2 Blocking: incubation with PEGASOS-Blocking Buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.3 Primary Antibody Incubation: incubation with anti-CD31 (1:200), anti-Claudin-5 (1:100), anti-GFAP (1:300) in PEGASOS-Labeling Buffer (5% (vol/vol) NGS, 0.5% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.4 Wash: incubation with PEGASOS-Wash Buffer (0.5% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
3.5 Secondary Antibody Incubation: incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–anti-rat (1:300), Alexa Fluor 488–anti-rabbit (1:300), Alexa Fluor 594–anti-mouse (1:300) in PEGASOS-Labeling Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  
3.6 Wash: incubation with PEGASOS-Wash Buffer (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes, protected from light)  
3.7 Nuclear Counterstain: incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PEGASOS-Wash Buffer) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.8 Final Wash: incubation with PEGASOS-Wash Buffer (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, protected from light)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Matching Solution A (40% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) PVP-40 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.42) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-Matching Solution B (60% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 1% (wt/vol) PVP-40 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with PEGASOS-Matching Solution C (80% (wt/vol) PEG-2000, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 2% (wt/vol) PVP-40 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with PEGASOS-Matching Solution C (Temperature: RT, store at 4 ℃ in dark until imaging)  
5.2 Equilibrate at RT for 2 hours before light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2.2 Repeat step 2.1 two more times with fresh PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that excels at preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) in thick tissues while minimizing fluorescence quenching and structural distortion—critical for sparse, weakly expressing neurons. It is compatible with immunolabeling of cytoskeletal markers like MAP2 to complement faint endogenous signals and recover fine dendritic arborization. CUBIC’s high refractive index matching (~1.49) enables deep imaging in 3 mm brain blocks, and samples can be stably stored in CUBIC-R+ for >6 months at 4 °C without significant signal loss or tissue degradation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 changes, 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Wash with PBS: 3 changes, 6 hours each (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) nicotinamide in ddH₂O; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)  

4 Long-Term Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in light-protected tube (Temperature: 4 ℃, Storage Duration: up to 6 months)  
4.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in CUBIC-R+ at RT for 12 hours (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that excels at preserving weak endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) over long-term storage, unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) which often quench or irreversibly damage such signals. It provides excellent transparency for 3 mm tissue blocks within days and enables stable refractive index (RI ≈ 1.49) matching compatible with light-sheet and confocal microscopy. The dual-labeling strategy leverages the sparse endogenous GFP reporter to identify individual neurons, while immunolabeling against MAP2 (a dendritic cytoskeletal marker) with Alexa Fluor 488 reinforces dendritic arborization and structural integrity; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial registration and cell density context. All fluorophores used are known to be well-preserved in CUBIC, and the cleared samples can be stored in CUBIC-R+ for ≥6 months without significant signal decay.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to confirm fixation completeness.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10 vol% Triton X-100, 10 vol% Tween-20, 10 wt% sucrose in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10 vol% DMSO, 5 vol% normal goat serum, 0.5 wt% sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with mouse anti-MAP2 primary antibody (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-B).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (0.5 vol% Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two additional times, changing solution every 8 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours total)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300 dilution in CUBIC-B).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Nuclear Counterstaining  
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in CUBIC-W).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Washing Prior to Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Tissue Clearing (Delipidation & Decolorization)  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 wt% Quadrol, 25 wt% urea, 15 wt% sucrose, 10 vol% Triton X-100 in H₂O, pH 9.0–9.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
8.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% triethanolamine, 0.5 vol% Triton X-100 in H₂O, RI = 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+ for final storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥6 months)  

10 Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC-R+ immediately before imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: <1 hour prior to acquisition)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a fructose-based, non-denaturing aqueous clearing method that excels at preserving weak endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) over long periods due to its reducing environment and absence of harsh organic solvents or high temperatures. It achieves high transparency in 3 mm brain blocks within days and provides excellent refractive index (RI ≈ 1.49) matching for high-resolution imaging. The addition of MAP2 immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor 488 complements sparse endogenous GFP by robustly labeling dendritic arbors without spectral overlap, enabling detailed morphological reconstruction. Alexa Fluor 488 is highly compatible with SeeDB2 and shows minimal quenching during long-term storage. This combination ensures both preservation of fragile intrinsic signal and structural completeness for dendritic analysis after 6 months.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to confirm fixation completeness.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling (MAP2)  
3.1 Incubation with anti-MAP2 primary antibody (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, changed every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days total)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800) in blocking solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  

6 Final Washes  
6.1 Incubation with 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS, changed every 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days total)  

7 Dehydration (Optional Pre-Clearing Rinse)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) fructose in PBS to equilibrate tissue before SeeDB2.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Optical Clearing with SeeDB2  
8.1 Incubation with SeeDB2 solution: 63.6% (wt/wt) fructose, 18.2% (wt/wt) α-thioglycerol, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-naphthylthiourea in 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

9 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
9.1 Transfer tissue into fresh SeeDB2 solution in light-protected glass vials with tight-sealing caps.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)  

10 Imaging Preparation (Prior to Acquisition)  
10.1 Equilibrate sample in fresh SeeDB2 at RT for 2 hours before mounting.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 647, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for large, lipid- and myelin-rich human brain tissues due to its strong delipidation capability via methanol dehydration and dichloromethane-based clearing, enabling deep penetration and uniform transparency in thick (5 mm) samples. It preserves protein epitopes well when combined with antigen retrieval, allowing robust immunolabeling of mature neuronal markers. NeuN specifically labels post-mitotic mature neurons across all cortical layers, while MAP2 highlights dendritic arbors, together providing complementary structural and population-level information essential for 3D neuron mapping, layer analysis, and density quantification. Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with iDISCO+’s organic solvents and offer high photostability and signal-to-noise for light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4.1 Incubation with pre-warmed 10 mM sodium citrate buffer (pH 6.0) at 80 ℃.(Temperature: 80 ℃, Time: 2 hours)

5.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

8.1 Wash with PBT (6 changes over 3 days, 12 hours per change).(Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)

9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

11 Refractive Index Matching

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly effective for lipid- and myelin-rich human brain tissue up to several millimeters thick, offering excellent transparency while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence. It uses aqueous reagents that support deep antibody penetration—critical for 5 mm human cortical slices—and is compatible with nuclear (DAPI) and protein epitope labeling (NeuN for mature neuronal nuclei; MAP2 for somatodendritic compartments). Dual labeling with NeuN and MAP2 enables robust identification of mature neurons by co-localization of nuclear and cytoplasmic signals, improving cell detection reliability in dense clinical tissue. CUBIC’s refractive index (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (Post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (5% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃ with gentle shaking, Time: 7 days)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 3 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃ with gentle shaking, Time: 5 days)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 3 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS: 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N-butanediol, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃ with gentle shaking, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Wash with PBS: 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  
2.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃ with gentle shaking, Time: 14 days)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (same composition as 2.3) for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Store samples in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. Samples are ready for light-sheet or confocal microscopy with objective correction collar set to RI ≈ 1.49.

**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly effective aqueous-based clearing method for thick, fixed human brain tissue, offering excellent antibody penetration (>3 mm), strong preservation of endogenous and immunofluorescent signals, and compatibility with nuclear/cytoplasmic neuronal markers. Unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), CUBIC minimizes fluorescence quenching of Alexa Fluor dyes and enables robust labeling in dense, lipid-rich human cortex. The dual-target strategy—NeuN (mature neuronal nuclei) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic cytoskeleton)—provides complementary spatial confirmation of mature neurons across cortical layers, significantly improving deep-tissue detection reliability compared to single markers. PBS dilution alone is insufficient for deep penetration; CUBIC’s high-pH, amino alcohol–based reagents enhance antibody diffusion while maintaining epitope integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (wt/vol) DMSO, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-NeuN (1:200) and rabbit anti-MAP2 (1:200) diluted in CUBIC-HL (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) Quadrol in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times with fresh CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 594 (1:400) diluted in CUBIC-HL (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) distilled water in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
7.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (fresh batch) until tissue becomes transparent and RI stabilizes (~1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  
8.2 Store sample in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. For light-sheet or confocal microscopy, mount directly in CUBIC-R+ within a glass-bottom chamber or agarose mold.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly effective aqueous-based clearing method for large, fixed human brain tissues, preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence while enabling deep antibody penetration through its strong delipidation and refractive index homogenization. Unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), CUBIC maintains protein epitopes better for immunolabeling in heavily fixed clinical samples. The dual labeling of NeuN (nuclear marker of mature neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic marker of mature neurons) provides complementary signals—nuclear localization for precise cell counting and cytoplasmic/dendritic signal for morphological confirmation—greatly enhancing reliability of deep neuron detection in dense 3 mm cortical tissue. Alexa Fluor dyes are chosen for their brightness, photostability, and compatibility with CUBIC’s high-pH environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (blocking buffer: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:200) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:200) diluted in CUBIC-A (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH ~10) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash with fresh CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Final wash with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) diluted in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Repeat wash with fresh CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.3 Final wash with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

7 Clearing (Delipidation and RI Homogenization)  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O, pH ~10) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
7.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O, RI = 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
8.2 Final incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥1 month)  
9.2 Mount directly in CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional dehydration or mounting media.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), tdTomato]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a rapid, methanol-based organic solvent clearing method optimized for fluorescence preservation of GFP and red fluorescent proteins (e.g., tdTomato) in fixed thick brain sections. It achieves high transparency in <24 hours while maintaining fine dendritic spine morphology—critical for spine density quantification. The method avoids harsh detergents or high temperatures that could quench endogenous fluorescence or distort delicate spines. Using sparse labeling with endogenous GFP (e.g., from Thy1-GFP-M line) combined with tdTomato (e.g., via AAV injection or transgenic expression) enables dual-color visualization of distinct neuronal populations or structural compartments, facilitating robust spine analysis without antibody penetration issues.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Fluorescence Protection and Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Optional Post-fixation (if needed for structural integrity)  
4.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) in dH₂O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) THF in dH₂O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma D103399).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)  

6 Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Mount cleared slice in glass-bottom imaging dish filled with DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)  
6.2 Seal edges with nail polish to prevent DBE evaporation during imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a rapid, aqueous-based optical clearing method optimized for preserving endogenous fluorescence (especially GFP/YFP) in fixed brain tissue up to 1 mm thick, with excellent compatibility for high-resolution imaging of fine neuronal structures like dendritic spines. **Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, DiI]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous-based, rapid optical clearing method optimized for preserving endogenous fluorescence (especially GFP/YFP) and compatible with lipophilic dyes like DiI. It achieves high transparency in thick brain slices (~500 μm) within hours, with minimal tissue distortion—critical for accurate dendritic spine morphometry. DiI labels neuronal membranes with high resolution of fine processes like spines, while endogenous or virally expressed GFP fills the cytoplasm, providing complementary structural context (e.g., dendritic shafts). SeeDB2 uses fructose-based refractive index (RI ≈ 1.49) matching, ideal for high-NA oil or silicone immersion objectives commonly used in confocal spine imaging, and completes full processing in <24 hours.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation (Assume PFA-fixed 500 μm mouse brain slices)  
1.1 Wash in PBS three times to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 DiI Labeling (if not pre-labeled)  
2.1 Incubate slices in 1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate (DiI, 5 μg/mL in PBS) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Wash thoroughly in PBS to remove unbound dye. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration (Optional but recommended for SeeDB2 compatibility)  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Optical Clearing with SeeDB2  
4.1 Incubation with SeeDB2-S (80.2% w/v fructose, 10% w/v α-thioglycerol, 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.5). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with SeeDB2-F (96.2% w/v fructose, 10% w/v α-thioglycerol, 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.5). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)

5.1 Transfer slices into fresh SeeDB2-F for final RI matching (RI ≈ 1.49). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mount samples between #1.5H coverslips using SeeDB2-F as mounting medium; seal edges with nail polish to prevent crystallization. (Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 48 hours)

**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament-H (SMI-32) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]

The method supports deep penetration of antibodies in intact tissue and achieves high transparency with refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet microscopy. We select β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) to label all immature neurons and growing axons, and Neurofilament-H (SMI-32) to highlight more mature neuronal processes and cranial/spinal nerve tracts; dual-color labeling enables discrimination of projection maturity and trajectory. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical context. Alexa Fluor 488/594 are chosen for their photostability and compatibility with iDISCO+ organic solvents.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament-H (SMI-32) + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole E12.5 mouse embryos (~8–10 mm) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of protein epitopes and fluorophores, and compatibility with antibody-based labeling—critical for visualizing both mature neurofilament-rich nerve bundles (via SMI-32) and early β-III tubulin–positive neurites. The method enables deep, low-background imaging in large samples and is optimized for light-sheet microscopy. TUJ1 labels all developing neurons and extending axons, while SMI-32 specifically highlights more mature, phosphorylated neurofilament-enriched tracts (e.g., cranial/spinal nerves), enabling dual-resolution analysis of neural connectivity maturation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous fluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-Neurofilament-H (SMI-32, e.g., BioLegend 801601, 1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (for TUJ1) and Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (for SMI-32), each at 1:500.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Repeat step 10.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

12 Storage / Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared embryo in DBE at RT in the dark; image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for Alexa Fluor 488 (ex ~488 nm, em ~519 nm) and Alexa Fluor 594 (ex ~590 nm, em ~617 nm).

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Synapsin]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is a rapid, aqueous-based optical clearing method specifically optimized for Drosophila tissues, including whole heads and brains with intact cuticle. It preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence exceptionally well, minimizes tissue distortion, and achieves high transparency within hours—critical for small (~0.5 mm) but chitin-rich samples like fly heads. The dual labeling of Bruchpilot (a core component of the presynaptic active zone) and Synapsin (a marker of synaptic vesicle clusters) enables precise spatial discrimination between active zones and surrounding vesicle pools, fulfilling the goal of mapping synapse density, distribution, and functional microdomains across neural circuits.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Primary Antibody Incubation  
1.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, Developmental Studies Hybridoma Bank, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (Synaptic Systems, 1:200) in FlyClear Blocking Buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with FlyClear Wash Buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

3 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibody mix: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in FlyClear Blocking Buffer. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with FlyClear Wash Buffer three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

5 Optical Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 45% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with FlyClear RI Matching Solution (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 53% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with FlyClear RI Matching Solution. Seal with coverslip using vacuum grease to prevent evaporation. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)
