**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for Drosophila tissues, effectively clearing chitinous cuticle while preserving fine synaptic structures and endogenous or immunolabeled fluorescence. It maintains high signal-to-background for antibody-based labeling in small brains (~0.5 mm) and is compatible with common Alexa Fluor dyes. BRP (nc82) labels the presynaptic active zone, while Synapsin marks synaptic vesicle clusters—enabling dual-channel discrimination of functionally distinct presynaptic domains. FlyClear’s mild, aqueous-based protocol avoids harsh organic solvents that could quench fluorescence or distort nanoscale architecture, making it ideal for high-resolution 3D imaging of synaptic organization across brain regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to confirm fixation completeness.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Blocking and Permeabilization  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, Developmental Studies Hybridoma Bank) at 1:50 dilution and rabbit anti-Synapsin (Synaptic Systems #102 002) at 1:200 dilution in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

6 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
6.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in blocking solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour, protected from light)  

8 Clearing with FlyClear  
8.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) sucrose, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (70% (wt/vol) fructose, 40% (wt/vol) sucrose, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Transfer sample to final RI-matching medium: FlyClear Imaging Buffer (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 40% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS; RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging, stored at 4 ℃ if not imaged immediately)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with FlyClear Imaging Buffer, sealed to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: 4 ℃ for storage up to 2 weeks; RT during imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82) + Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is specifically optimized for Drosophila tissues, including those with intact cuticle, and effectively clears chitinous exoskeletons while preserving fine synaptic structures and endogenous/immunofluorescence signals. It outperforms SeeDB2 in cuticle penetration and provides superior transparency for whole heads or dissected brains ≤0.5 mm. The chosen markers—Bruchpilot (a core component of the presynaptic active zone) and Synapsin (associated with synaptic vesicle clusters)—enable dual-channel discrimination of functionally distinct presynaptic domains. Alexa Fluor dyes offer high photostability and compatibility with FlyClear’s organic solvent-based protocol, minimizing background and maximizing signal-to-noise for 3D circuit mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS to reverse Bouin’s-induced crosslinks and stabilize epitopes.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with PBT containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) and 2% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) diluted in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

3 Primary Antibody Wash  
3.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour)  

4 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated goat anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) in PBT + 5% NGS, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 1 hour, protected from light)  

6 Dehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

7 FlyClear Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with FlyClear solution (1:2 mixture of benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate, BABB) containing 0.1% (wt/vol) n-propyl gallate (antifade).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh FlyClear (BABB + 0.1% n-propyl gallate) in glass-bottom imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
8.2 Seal chamber with coverslip using VALAP or nail polish to prevent evaporation during imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at 4 ℃ in dark for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 488, Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized hard tissues such as neonatal mouse calvaria, enabling efficient delipidation and decalcification while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody-based signals. It achieves high transparency in small bone blocks (~5 mm) within days without harsh organic solvents that quench fluorophores. The dual-marker strategy targets key stages of osteoblast lineage: Osterix (Osx) labels early osteoprogenitors and pre-osteoblasts, while Osteocalcin marks mature, matrix-embedded osteoblasts/osteocytes. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial registration. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of differentiation gradients across the suture mesenchyme, osteogenic fronts, and adjacent bone plates during postnatal calvarial growth.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

It minimizes tissue distortion—critical for precise spatial analysis of suture microarchitecture—and effectively reduces bone autofluorescence. The dual-marker strategy targets early osteoprogenitors (Osterix/Osx) and mature osteoblasts (Osteocalcin), allowing clear distinction of differentiation stages across suture zones. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for 3D registration. Alexa Fluor dyes are photostable and compatible with BoneClear’s organic solvent-based protocol.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration

1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with BoneClear Reagent A (10% (wt/vol) EDTA, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.5% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)

3.1 Rehydration: sequential incubation in 70%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, 30 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  
3.2 Permeabilization and blocking: incubation with blocking buffer (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-Osterix (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osterix (Osx)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 594, CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized hard tissues such as neonatal mouse calvaria, enabling efficient lipid removal and decalcification while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody penetration—critical for imaging bone suture microarchitecture. The dual osteolineage markers Osx (early osteoprogenitors) and Osteocalcin (mature osteoblasts) allow spatial discrimination of differentiation stages across suture zones. CD31 labels vascular endothelium to assess angiogenesis–osteogenesis coupling, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for 3D cell localization. BoneClear’s EDTA-based decalcification and mild detergent conditions preserve protein epitopes better than harsh organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), which is essential for reliable immunolabeling in P7 calvarial bone.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Decalcification (BoneClear Step 1)  
2.1 Incubation with BoneClear Decalcification Solution (10% (wt/vol) EDTA, 0.5% (wt/vol) SDS in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

3 Immunolabeling Preparation  
3.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with Blocking Buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer (1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS): anti-Osterix (1:200), anti-Osteocalcin (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Washing  
5.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Repeat PBST wash (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Repeat PBST wash (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 594, and Alexa Fluor 647 (all 1:500) plus DAPI (1 µg/mL) in Antibody Dilution Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

7 Post-labeling Washes  
7.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
7.2 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)  

8 Optical Clearing (BoneClear Step 2)  
8.1 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution A (20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP, MW 40 kDa), 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution B (40% (wt/vol) sucrose, 20% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI Matching Solution (63% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep™), 10% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS; final RI ≈ 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample into fresh BoneClear RI Matching Solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber (Temperature: 4 ℃, storage until imaging; image within 7 days)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (凝集素) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for clearing dense, lipid-rich tissues such as bone and preserves endogenous fluorescence and immunolabeling signals robustly. It enables deep penetration of antibodies into intact mouse femurs (~15 mm) and achieves high transparency with refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet microscopy. TH is the rate-limiting enzyme in norepinephrine synthesis and a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers; Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) labels functional vasculature in bone marrow; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context. Alexa Fluor 488 and 594 offer photostable, spectrally distinct signals compatible with iDISCO+’s organic solvent-based protocol.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: anti-TH (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody mix: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:200) + Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin, 10 µg/mL) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 + DAPI (1 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, with gentle shaking)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day, with 4 buffer changes)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer sample to fresh 100% DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store cleared femur in DBE at RT in the dark. Mount vertically in a glass capillary or chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal imaging (RI ≈ 1.56).

2.1 Incubation with BoneClear Solution A (10% (wt/vol) EDTA, 0.5% (wt/vol) SDS, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 48 hours)

3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100), and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace antibody solution every 3 days)  
3.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)

3.7 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

我在进行小鼠股骨骨髓透明化实验时遇到问题：组织在叔丁醇梯度 70% 步骤后变得非常脆，后续操作中容易碎裂，导致完整股骨结构和骨髓腔空间连续性被破坏。此前流程为固定和免疫标记后，直接按照 BoneClear protocol 进行处理。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法，使其适合完整股骨硬组织透明化、骨髓腔结构保留、交感神经纤维和血管/周细胞结构双信号检测，以及低脆裂风险的三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的双靶点荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (凝集素) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone, preserving both mineralized matrix integrity and endogenous/immunolabeled fluorescence while minimizing brittleness through polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based dehydration and refractive index matching. Unlike alcohol-based methods (e.g., BoneClear, iDISCO+), it avoids harsh methanol/tert-butanol steps that cause cracking in dense cortical bone and fragile marrow cavities. The dual vascular labeling (CD31 for endothelial cells + Lectin for perfused vasculature) ensures comprehensive vessel detection, while TH robustly labels sympathetic nerve fibers. DAPI provides nuclear context without interfering with bone autofluorescence. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are highly stable under PEGASOS conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) PEG 200 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) PEG 200 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) PEG 200 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling (if not pre-labeled; skip if already stained post-fixation)  
2.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-TH (1:200) + anti-CD31 (1:100) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
2.4 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  
2.5 Secondary antibody + Lectin incubation: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) + Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-rat IgG (1:300) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (10 μg/mL) in blocking buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking)  
2.6 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  
2.7 Nuclear counterstain: DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.8 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Delipidation & Decalcification (mild, integrated)  
3.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A solution (10% (wt/vol) PEG 200, 5% (wt/vol) EDTA, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-B1 (40% (wt/vol) PEG 200, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-B2 (60% (wt/vol) PEG 200, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with PEGASOS-C (80% (wt/vol) PEG 200, 70% (wt/vol) sorbitol, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with PEGASOS-C (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Mount intact femur vertically in glass capillary or custom holder submerged in PEGASOS-C for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI matched, no additional mounting medium required).

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并匹配适合完整耳蜗硬组织成像的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的荧光探针可以直接回答部分科学目标，则优先使用该探针而不是额外选择抗体。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin, Myosin VIIa]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as the otic capsule surrounding the mouse cochlea, enabling efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving endogenous fluorescence and fine F-actin structures. It achieves high transparency in mineralized samples without requiring harsh delipidation that could disrupt delicate stereocilia bundles. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin–rich stereocilia and cuticular plates of hair cells, fulfilling the need to assess bundle integrity and spatial organization without additional antibodies where possible. Myosin VIIa is a highly specific marker for cochlear hair cells (both inner and outer), enabling unambiguous identification and automated counting across the entire spiral. This combination allows direct 3D quantification of hair cell loss and stereocilia damage along the tonotopic axis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) to ensure complete fixation after dissection.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with BoneClear-Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, 0.1 M NaOH, pH adjusted to 7.4 with HCl) with gentle agitation.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 days)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Immunolabeling and Cytoskeletal Staining  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 4 changes)  
3.4 Incubation with fluorescent secondary antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG, 1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 4 changes)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

5 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear-Clearing Solution A (10% (wt/vol) N-lauroylsarcosine sodium salt in 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with BoneClear-Clearing Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with BoneClear-Mounting Solution (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 12% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Final Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample into fresh BoneClear-Mounting Solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched RI glass vial.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 2 weeks for optimal signal)

我需要对小鼠耳蜗进行透明化处理，用于全耳蜗毛细胞计数和噪音损伤评估。样本为完整小鼠耳蜗，深埋于致密听泡骨中，呈螺旋状，大小约 3 mm × 2 mm × 2 mm，已完成固定和后固定。科学目标是在完整耳蜗尺度下同时识别毛细胞身份和毛细胞 F-actin/静纤毛束结构，分析噪音损伤后内外毛细胞缺失、排列紊乱、静纤毛束破坏和不同螺旋区域的损伤梯度。

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor conjugate, Myosin VIIa primary antibody + Alexa Fluor secondary, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues like bone-encased cochleae, combining effective decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching in a single workflow while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunoreactivity. It outperforms BoneClear in bone transparency and signal retention for cytoskeletal and protein epitopes. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles with high specificity; Myosin VIIa is the gold-standard marker for both inner and outer hair cells across all cochlear turns; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cell counting and spatial registration. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are compatible with PEGASOS and resistant to quenching during clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification & Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A1 (8% (wt/vol) EDTA, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Repeat wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking solution) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 or 568 (1:100 in blocking solution) + DAPI (1 µg/mL) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours, gentle agitation)  
3.3 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
3.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibody (1:400 in blocking solution, matching host species of primary) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle agitation)  
3.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.5 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Delipidation & Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

6 Rehydration  
6.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.4 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-B (50% (wt/vol) PEG-400, 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in water, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-C (80% (wt/vol) PEG-400, 20% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide in water, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Storage & Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with PEGASOS-C and seal (Temperature: 4 ℃, long-term storage); for imaging, equilibrate at RT for 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a high-refractive-index aqueous-based clearing method that effectively clears mineralized tissues like teeth while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals. It is compatible with immunolabeling of small, dense samples such as mouse molars (~2 mm) and maintains structural integrity of enamel and dentin. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels all nerve fibers in the pulp, while tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) specifically marks sympathetic fibers, enabling discrimination of sympathetic vs. general neural innervation. Both targets require antibody-based detection, which CUBIC supports robustly due to its strong delipidation and permeabilization properties without decalcification.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for gentle rehydration and detergent permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in CUBIC Ab diluent (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS): anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), anti-TH (1:300).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with PBST (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) to remove unbound primary antibodies.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-rabbit or anti-mouse as appropriate for PGP9.5 host) and Alexa Fluor 594 (for TH host), each at 1:500 dilution in CUBIC Ab diluent.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-labeling Wash  
5.1 Incubation with PBST (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

6 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in distilled water) for delipidation and initial clearing.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.52) for final refractive index matching.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Transfer sample into fresh CUBIC-R+ for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store cleared tooth in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark for long-term preservation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
8.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, IB4]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly effective aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is compatible with lipophilic tracers like DiI and lectin-based labeling such as IB4. It provides excellent transparency for mineralized tissues like teeth when combined with appropriate decalcification (which is not required here since the goal is structural preservation of enamel/dentin and the sample is small). DiI is a carbocyanine membrane dye that diffuses along neuronal membranes and reliably labels entire axonal trajectories from injection or immersion sites—ideal for tracing nerve entry at the root apex into the pulp. IB4 (isolectin B4) binds specifically to non-peptidergic sensory nerve terminals and complements DiI by highlighting terminal arborizations in the pulp without requiring antibodies. Both dyes are chemically stable under CUBIC reagents, avoiding the need for immunolabeling and preserving fine 3D architecture of the pulp cavity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fluorescent Labeling  
1.1 Incubation with 5 µg/mL DiI (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) with 0.1% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Wash with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Incubation with 10 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 in 0.1 M phosphate buffer containing 1 mM CaCl₂ and 1 mM MgCl₂.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (CUBIC)  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (w/v) N-butanediol, 10% (w/v) sucrose, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.5) for delipidation and initial clearing.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBS (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
2.4 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (w/v) sucrose, 25% (w/v) urea, 10% (w/v) triethanolamine, 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100, adjusted to RI ≈ 1.49 with distilled water) for refractive index matching.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Final RI Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to glass vial with fresh CUBIC-R+ and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)

IB4 specifically labels sensory nerve fibers in dental pulp (binds to α-D-galactose residues on non-myelinated neurons), Phalloidin highlights F-actin in soft tissue boundaries and cellular architecture of the pulp, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context. This combination enables clear visualization of neural distribution relative to pulp morphology without requiring transgenic labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA aqueous solution, pH 7.4, with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Repeat wash with fresh PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Permeabilization and Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Immunolabeling (Direct Staining)  
4.1 Incubation with staining solution: 10 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4, 5 U/mL Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin, and 5 µg/mL DAPI in CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Repeat wash with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Optical Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial with fresh CUBIC-R+ for imaging or long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4 (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is a rapid, non-dehydration-based aqueous clearing method optimized for mineralized tissues like teeth and bone, preserving endogenous fluorescence and soft tissue morphology without causing significant shrinkage or distortion of the pulp cavity—addressing the key issue of pulp contraction observed with BoneClear. It maintains high transparency while retaining delicate neural and vascular structures within hard tissues. IB4 labels vasculature and some sensory nerve fibers in dental pulp; TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) specifically marks neuronal processes, enabling visualization of nerve entry and branching from the apical foramen; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for soft tissue context. All fluorophores are compatible with Ce3D’s mild pH and low-detergent conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (Perform after fixation/post-fixation, before clearing)  
1.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 24 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) + IB4 (10 µg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
1.4 Washing with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS, 6 changes over 48 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in blocking buffer (IB4 is directly conjugated, no secondary needed).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Final wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS, 6 changes over 48 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
1.7 Post-staining nuclear counterstain: incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) for 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.8 Final rinse with PBS, 3 changes over 6 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A solution (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water, pH 7.5) for 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh Ce3D-A solution for additional 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water, pH 7.5) for 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Transfer samples to Ce3D-Matching Solution (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) for 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Replace with fresh Ce3D-Matching Solution and incubate until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥6 hours, store at RT in dark)  

4 Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Mount cleared tooth in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution, oriented for apical access view.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissue–soft tissue composites (e.g., bone–muscle–nerve), enabling efficient delipidation and decalcification while preserving endogenous fluorescence and lipophilic dye signals. It achieves high transparency in mineralized tissues without requiring harsh decalcification that damages fine neural structures. DiI is a lipophilic carbocyanine dye that stably incorporates into neuronal membranes and retrogradely/anterogradely labels entire axonal trajectories—including fine peripheral branches—without requiring antibodies or transgenic expression, satisfying the constraint to avoid unnecessary antibody labeling. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical context. PEGASOS maintains DiI and DAPI fluorescence well and matches RI to ~1.52, compatible with high-NA oil or silicone-oil objectives for light-sheet or confocal imaging of 10-mm samples.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Pre-Clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 DiI Neural Tract Labeling (if not pre-labeled; skip if already labeled during perfusion/post-fixation)  
2.1 Microinjection or focal application of 1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate (DiI, 2 mg/mL in DMSO) onto exposed nerve roots or cut nerve ends under stereomicroscope.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes application)  
2.2 Incubation in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS for dye stabilization.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Post-labeling wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

4 Decalcification & Delipidation (PEGASOS Reagent A)  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS Reagent A (8% (wt/vol) tetrahydrofuran, 10% (wt/vol) formamide, 10% (vol/vol) dimethyl sulfoxide, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium dodecyl sulfate, 0.1 M EDTA, pH 7.5) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

5 Bleaching (Optional, only if strong autofluorescence observed)  
5.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Rehydration through methanol series: 70%, 50%, 30% methanol in PBS, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

6 Nuclear Counterstaining  
6.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

7 Dehydration (Post-staining)  
7.1 Repeat steps 3.1–3.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: as in Step 3)  

8 Refractive Index Matching (PEGASOS Reagent B → C)  
8.1 Incubation with PEGASOS Reagent B (50% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PEGASOS Reagent C (80% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 5% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4, RI ≈ 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

9 Final Equilibration and Storage  
9.1 Transfer sample to fresh PEGASOS Reagent C in glass vial, sealed to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 4 weeks for optimal DiI signal)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, MBP + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues including bone and cartilage while preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration—critical for the mouse vertebral column with dense mineralized matrix. It effectively clears both bone and soft tissue components in a single protocol, allowing 3D visualization of neural structures traversing bony foramina and muscle. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels all peripheral nerve fibers, while MBP (myelin basic protein) selectively highlights myelinated axons, enabling direct comparison of total vs. thickly myelinated fiber distributions. Alexa Fluor 488 and 594 are highly compatible with PEGASOS due to their photostability and resistance to organic solvent-induced quenching during clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification  
2.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A1 solution (10% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) tetrahydrofuran, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium dodecyl sulfate, 0.1 M EDTA, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh PEGASOS-A1 solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Permeabilization with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Blocking with PBS + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Primary antibody incubation: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-MBP (1:300) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.4 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 6 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 18 hours total)

6.2 Incubation with fresh PEGASOS-B1.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues (bone, cartilage) combined with soft tissues (muscle, nerve), enabling deep clearing of mineralized and fibrous structures while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals. It effectively removes lipids and decalcifies mildly without destroying fine neural architecture. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in muscle fibers, providing high-resolution cytoskeletal reference without requiring additional antibodies; TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) robustly labels peripheral nerve fibers and their branches. This dual-labeling strategy fulfills the requirement to visualize both neural trajectories and muscle structural context in 3D within a bone-muscle-nerve composite.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Repeat incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification  
2.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A solution (10% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 5% (wt/vol) tetrahydrofuran, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium dodecyl sulfate, 0.1 M EDTA, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-B solution (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) mouse monoclonal antibody diluted 1:500 in PEGASOS-C staining buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 5% (wt/vol) normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-W wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash with PEGASOS-W.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated goat anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) in PEGASOS-C staining buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Final Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-W wash buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-M1 (47% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-M2 (63% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide, RI ≈ 1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to fresh PEGASOS-M2 in imaging chamber with refractive index–matched coverslip or glass-bottom dish.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimized for whole-body clearing of adult mice, provides excellent preservation of red-shifted fluorescent proteins like mCherry/RFP, and enables deep-tissue immunolabeling with high penetration. Its organic solvent–based protocol effectively removes lipids while maintaining endogenous fluorescence and allowing robust antibody penetration in dense tissues such as bone marrow and lung—key sites for breast cancer metastasis. CK19 is a well-established epithelial cytokeratin marker specific to carcinoma cells, including breast cancer, and pairing it with Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red) avoids spectral overlap with mCherry (emission ~610 nm), enabling reliable dual-channel validation of micro-metastases at single-cell resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [mCherry (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimized for whole adult mouse clearing with excellent preservation of red-shifted fluorescent proteins like mCherry/RFP, which are critical for tracking tumor cells. It efficiently clears dense tissues including bone and brain while maintaining endogenous fluorescence—essential for detecting sparse micro-metastases across multiple organs. The protocol includes optional immunolabeling compatible with methanol-based processing; we add Pan-Cytokeratin (a pan-epithelial marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to confirm epithelial origin of mCherry+ signals and exclude false positives from autofluorescence or non-tumor RFP-like signals. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly stable in iDISCO+ and spectrally separable from mCherry.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, only if high tissue autofluorescence observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (Pan-Cytokeratin)  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing rat anti-Pan-Cytokeratin antibody (e.g., BioLegend, clone TROMA-1) at 1:200 dilution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:500 dilution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample in 100% DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount whole mouse in a custom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56).

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (TRITC- or Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a highly effective dehydration-based clearing method optimized for large, pigmented tissues such as melanoma. It efficiently removes lipids and reduces light scattering while preserving endogenous and exogenous fluorescence over weeks to months. Crucially, uDISCO includes a strong bleaching step using H₂O₂ in methanol that effectively quenches melanin’s optical interference—addressing the core challenge of black pigment–induced absorption and scattering in melanoma. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) binds specifically to glycoproteins on vascular endothelial luminal surfaces, enabling direct, high-contrast labeling of the entire perfusable microvasculature without requiring antibody penetration into dense tumor tissue. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context. This combination avoids reliance on fragile fluorescent proteins or deep antibody penetration, which is hindered in melanin-rich, fibrotic tumors.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Initial Fixation (assumed complete per problem statement; proceed from post-fixed tumor block)  
1.1 Ensure tumor tissue (8–10 mm diameter) is post-fixed in 4% PFA in PBS for 24 hours at 4 ℃ prior to clearing. Rinse 3 × 30 min in PBS before starting protocol.  

2 Vascular Labeling with Lectin  
2.1 Incubate tumor in lectin solution: 50 µg/mL TRITC- or Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin in PBS containing 1 mM CaCl₂ and 1 mM MnCl₂. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.2 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 1 hour in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT)  

3 Nuclear Counterstaining  
3.1 Incubate in 5 µg/mL DAPI in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Wash: 3 × 1 hour in PBST. (Temperature: RT)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Melanin Bleaching  
5.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–24 hours; monitor until tissue turns pale beige/tan)  

6 Delipidation  
6.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Repeat DCM incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Final incubation in fresh 100% DBE for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until fully transparent and RI-matched, RI ≈ 1.56)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store cleared tumor in glass vial filled with DBE at RT in the dark. Samples remain stable for >6 months.  
8.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy using long-working-distance objectives (e.g., 2×/0.5 NA or 10×/0.6 NA water-dipping objective with DBE correction collar if available).

请根据该科学问题选择兼容的荧光/标记策略，并选择与这些信号兼容的组织透明方法。若直接血管腔面探针能够回答灌流功能问题，应优先作为功能性血管通道；若要判断内皮结构完整性，则从给定标记物列表中选择血管内皮相关靶点。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for clearing pigmented tissues like melanoma due to its strong delipidation and bleaching steps that reduce melanin-induced light scattering and autofluorescence. It preserves protein epitopes sufficiently for antibody labeling post-fixation and is compatible with both lectin-based vascular perfusion labeling (for functional vasculature) and anti-CD31 immunostaining (for structural endothelial networks). Lectin injected intravascularly prior to fixation specifically labels perfused vessel lumens, while CD31 reveals all endothelial structures regardless of perfusion status. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tumor architecture context. iDISCO+’s organic solvent–based refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.52) enables deep imaging in light-sheet or confocal microscopy with high signal-to-noise even in melanin-rich regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Pre-Clearing Preparation (Assume already completed: tumor fixed by transcardial perfusion with 4% PFA, followed by post-fixation in 4% PFA for 2 h at 4 ℃; intravascular lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 perfused prior to fixation)  
1.1 Wash tissue in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Bleaching (to reduce melanin absorption and autofluorescence)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBST (PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Blocking and Permeabilization  
5.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining (anti-CD31 for structural endothelium)  
6.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 primary antibody diluted 1:200 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

7 Washing  
7.1 Wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

8 Secondary Antibody Staining  
8.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 diluted 1:500 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

9 Post-Staining Washes  
9.1 Wash with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
9.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dehydration (pre-clearing for organic solvents)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation and Clearing  
11.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in DBE up to 1 week)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a rapid, aqueous-based clearing method compatible with immunolabeling and preserves protein epitopes well, making it ideal for fixed clinical biopsy samples requiring antibody-based detection of epithelial markers. Pan-Cytokeratin robustly labels all epithelial cells—including carcinoma cells—in breast tissue and is routinely used in pathology to confirm epithelial origin; conjugation to Alexa Fluor 488 ensures bright, photostable fluorescence compatible with CUBIC’s high-refractive-index reagents. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context and identification of cellular morphology near margins. CUBIC achieves full transparency of 5 mm³ tissue blocks within 24–48 hours, aligning with the near-intraoperative timeframe requirement.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (Perform on PFA-fixed, post-fixed tissue)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: mouse anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 × 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (2 × 30 minutes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

2 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)-2-aminoethanesulfonic acid (BES), 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (vol/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE) in distilled water, pH 9.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (same composition) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 0.1% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (same composition) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 7 days)

CK19 and Pan-Cytokeratin are robust epithelial/tumor markers for breast carcinoma identification; dual labeling enhances specificity for residual cancer nests. DAPI provides nuclear reference to assess spatial relationship to cut margins. CUBIC’s RI (~1.49) matches standard light-sheet/confocal objectives and avoids organic solvents that quench fluorescence.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in ethanol or dehydrated)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CK19 (1:200) and anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.02% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)

5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594 anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour, protected from light)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a rapid, aqueous-based clearing method compatible with formaldehyde-fixed tissues and preserves protein epitopes well, enabling robust immunolabeling of epithelial markers like Pan-Cytokeratin—critical for identifying residual carcinoma cells. It achieves high transparency in <24 h for small biopsies (≤5 mm) and matches well with nuclear counterstain DAPI for spatial reference to tissue architecture and true margin. Unlike FOCM (which failed to clear adequately), CUBIC’s high-concentration amino alcohol reagents effectively remove lipids and homogenize refractive index without harsh dehydration, preserving fluorescence and morphology essential for clinical margin assessment within the 24–48 h window.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (Perform after fixation/post-fixation; assume tissue is in PBS)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: mouse anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 16 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400 in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.7 Final wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (CUBIC protocol adapted for rapid processing)  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (w/v) Quadrol, 25% (w/v) urea, 15% (w/v) sucrose, 10% (v/v) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 50% (v/v) CUBIC-L in ddH₂O (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (w/v) sucrose, 25% (w/v) urea, 10% (w/v) α-thioglycerol in ddH₂O, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer tissue into fresh CUBIC-R+ for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (no additional mounting medium required)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 488, p63+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunofluorescence signals exceptionally well in fixed human biopsy tissues, including dense epithelial organs like the prostate. It is compatible with standard antibody labeling and allows deep penetration in millimeter-scale samples without harsh organic solvents that could damage delicate glandular architecture. CK19 labels luminal epithelial cells (including malignant ones), while p63 specifically marks basal cells; their combined signal enables unambiguous identification of intact vs. disrupted basal layers—a key criterion for Gleason pattern assessment. DAPI provides nuclear context to delineate gland contours and cellular packing but is not used alone for diagnostic calls, aligning with the problem constraints.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 reagent (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B reagent (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with anti-CK19 (mouse monoclonal, 1:200) and anti-p63 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:200) diluted in CUBIC-B + 5% NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash step 4.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in CUBIC-B + 5% NGS (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours each, protected from light)  

7 Nuclear Counterstain  
7.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in CUBIC-B) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, protected from light)  

9 Clearing with CUBIC-L  
9.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (10% (wt/vol) N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)-2-aminoethanesulfonic acid (BES), 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sodium polyacrylate, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, pH 9.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

11 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 4 ℃, storage until imaging; image within 7 days)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [MECA-79 (anti-HEV addressin) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Hoechst 33342]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, especially for delicate epitopes like HEV addressins (recognized by MECA-79). It is ideal for small (~2–3 mm) lymphoid tissues such as inguinal lymph nodes, enabling deep, uniform labeling and imaging without delipidation-induced antigen loss. The combination of MECA-79 (specific for sulfated sialomucins on HEVs) and pan-endothelial CD31 allows precise discrimination of HEV segments from general vasculature. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain to assess lymphocyte density gradients across cortical, paracortical, and medullary zones without interfering with green/red channels. CUBIC’s RI (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-MECA-79 (1:100) and rat anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in CUBIC-A (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Wash with CUBIC-W (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times with solution change every 2 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-rat IgM Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and goat anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200), plus Hoechst 33342 (1:1000), all diluted in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-Staining Wash  
5.1 Wash with CUBIC-W (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 3 times with solution change every 2 hours)  

6 Tissue Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (Reagent 1: 25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (Reagent 2: 50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) Quadrol in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer cleared lymph node into a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [MECA-79 (anti-HEV) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method ideal for small, fixed immune organs like mouse inguinal lymph nodes (2–3 mm). It preserves protein epitopes and fluorescent signals effectively, enabling high-quality immunolabeling of delicate vascular structures such as high endothelial venules (HEVs). MECA-79 is the gold-standard antibody for HEV-specific sulfated glycans and will precisely label the HEV network. CD31 (PECAM1) provides pan-endothelial context to distinguish HEVs from other vasculature. DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain to delineate lymphocyte-dense cortical, paracortical, and medullary zones without requiring additional cell-type-specific markers, aligning with the goal of spatial mapping relative to cellular architecture. CUBIC’s refractive index (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives and avoids organic solvents that could quench Alexa Fluor dyes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-MECA-79 (1:100) and rat anti-CD31 (1:100) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBT) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and Alexa Fluor 594 (1:200), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes, protected from light)  

7 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
