**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD19+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ immunolabeling and clearing of mouse spleen (~15 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of protein epitopes for antibody penetration, and compatibility with organic-soluble fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. B220 and CD19 are pan-B cell markers that robustly label B cell follicles in white pulp; dual labeling enhances specificity and signal intensity. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture without interfering with B cell signal. iDISCO+’s methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane/DBE-based RI matching yield high transparency and low autofluorescence in lymphoid tissue, enabling high-resolution 3D imaging of follicular organization along the splenic axes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for spleen autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-mouse B220 (PTPRC, BioLegend, clone RA3-6B2) at 1:200 and rat anti-mouse CD19 (BioLegend, clone 6D5) at 1:200 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, change buffer every 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (for B220) and Alexa Fluor 594 (for CD19), each at 1:500, in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) heparin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, change buffer every 6 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 three times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with 5 µg/mL DAPI in PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
9.2 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Repeat step 11.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
12.2 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in glass vial for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, Ki67+Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (Lycopersicon esculentum)+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is ideal for fixed murine spleen (~15 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation and protein preservation capabilities in aqueous conditions, which maintains endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes better than organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+). It enables deep, uniform clearing of lymphoid organs while preserving B-cell markers. B220 robustly labels all B cells; Ki67 identifies proliferating cells within vaccine-induced germinal centers (GCs); Lycopersicon esculentum lectin binds GC-associated stromal networks and follicular dendritic cells, providing structural context for GC localization; DAPI labels nuclei for segmentation and spatial reference. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series + DAPI) are highly compatible with CUBIC’s high-pH reagents and RI-matching solutions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for gentle permeabilization.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Antibody and Lectin Staining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-B220 (1:200), anti-Ki67 (1:100), and Lycopersicon esculentum lectin (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400), and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated streptavidin (if biotinylated lectin used; otherwise direct conjugate at 1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.5 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total, with 3 buffer changes every 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Washing with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, with one buffer change)

4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE) in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite)  
5.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh CUBIC-R+ for 1 hour at RT to minimize bubbles and ensure optical homogeneity.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD35 (CR1/2)+Alexa Fluor 647, Ki67+Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (Lycopersicon esculentum)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-organic solvent clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals exceptionally well in immunologically active tissues like spleen. It effectively clears lipid-rich but structurally delicate lymphoid organs without causing significant tissue shrinkage or distortion—critical for accurate 3D morphometry of B cell follicles and germinal centers. The chosen labeling strategy targets: B220 to delineate all B cells and white pulp follicles; CD35 to specifically label follicular dendritic cell networks within germinal centers; Ki67 to identify proliferating cells in active germinal center reactions; tomato lectin to visualize marginal zone and red pulp vasculature/sinus architecture; and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining to assess cellular density and spatial context. All fluorophores are compatible with CUBIC’s high-pH reagents and RI-matching solutions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.05% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-B220 (1:200), anti-CD35 (1:100), anti-Ki67 (1:100) diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.05% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody + Lectin + Nuclear Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rat IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rat IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-rabbit IgG (1:400); plus Lycopersicon esculentum Lectin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (10 µg/mL); plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC-L  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N-benzyl-2-methylbenzamide (NBM), 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, pH 9.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) iohexol, 10% (wt/vol) NBM, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, pH 7.5, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

9 Storage / Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Store cleared spleen immersed in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 2 weeks; equilibrate to RT for 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal imaging.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD35 (CR1/2)+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimal for intact, lipid-rich and highly pigmented organs like the spleen due to its robust methanol-based dehydration, strong delipidation with dichloromethane (DCM), and effective hemoglobin decolorization via H₂O₂ in methanol. It preserves protein epitopes better than harsh organic solvents used in uDISCO/FDISCO and enables deep antibody penetration in mm-scale tissues. B220 labels all B cells to delineate follicles; CD35 (not listed but implied as standard for germinal centers—however, per constraints we must use only allowed markers; thus we substitute with **Ki67+Alexa Fluor 647** as a surrogate for active germinal center B cells, since Ki67 marks proliferating centroblasts in GCs) — correction: among allowed markers, **Ki67 (MKI67)** is available and is a well-established marker for germinal center reaction intensity. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context. This combination allows 3D quantification of follicle volume (B220⁺), GC activity (Ki67⁺ within B220⁺ zones), and spatial mapping in white pulp.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-B220 (PTPRC) rat monoclonal antibody (e.g., RA3-6B2, 1:200) and anti-Ki67 (MKI67) rabbit polyclonal antibody (1:100) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes every 4 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rat IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes every 4 hours)  
8.2 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of methanol:dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Nuclear Counterstaining (optional post-clearing DAPI if signal lost)  
12.1 Incubation with 10 µg/mL DAPI in DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Transfer spleen to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, ready for light-sheet or confocal imaging)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for fixed, intact mouse tumor tissues (~8 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence (especially Alexa Fluor dyes), and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. It enables deep penetration of antibodies into dense tumor stroma and provides high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.52) suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging. The labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: CD3 labels all T cells, CD8 identifies cytotoxic T cell subset, CD31 outlines vasculature for spatial reference, and DAPI provides nuclear context to delineate tumor architecture (e.g., necrotic core vs. viable rim).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

11.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3 + Alexa Fluor 488, CD8 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimal for fixed, intact solid tumors (~8 mm) due to its strong delipidation and refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.56), enabling deep imaging into dense tumor cores. The dual labeling of pan-T cells (CD3) and cytotoxic T cells (CD8) with spectrally distinct, photostable Alexa Fluor conjugates allows precise 3D subpopulation discrimination. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial registration without interfering with T cell channels. The original protocol failed due to insufficient methanol dehydration (only 1 h per step) and omission of H₂O₂-based decoloration; the revised protocol corrects both to enhance penetration, reduce background, and recover core signal.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decoloration  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% donkey serum, 10% DMSO, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CD3 (e.g., clone 17A2, 1:200) and anti-CD8 (e.g., clone 53-6.7, 1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, 3% donkey serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rat IgG (for CD3) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (for CD8), each at 1:500, in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Nuclear Counterstain  
9.1 Incubation with DAPI (5 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
9.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Dehydration (post-staining)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching

12.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

13 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in airtight glass vial wrapped in aluminum foil at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 647, cTnT + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** The mouse cardiac conduction system—particularly Purkinje fibers—is best labeled by the combination of Cx40 (connexin 40) and Hcn4 (hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated channel 4), which are established molecular markers for the proximal and distal components of the specialized conduction network, including Purkinje fibers. Co-staining with cTnT (cardiac troponin T) provides high-contrast delineation of cardiomyocyte architecture to contextualize Purkinje fiber distribution within ventricular walls. iDISCO+ is selected because it effectively clears dense, lipid-rich tissues like adult mouse heart, efficiently removes hemoglobin (reducing background from blood remnants), preserves protein epitopes for immunolabeling, and achieves high transparency with excellent compatibility for Alexa Fluor dyes. Its organic solvent–based refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.52) is ideal for high-resolution light-sheet imaging of whole hearts (~10 mm scale).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 488, Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, which is critical for dual-channel immunolabeling of delicate protein epitopes like Cx40 (a key gap junction protein in the cardiac conduction system) and Cntn2 (Contactin-2), a validated marker for Purkinje fibers in mouse heart. Unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), CUBIC minimizes fluorophore quenching and maintains tissue integrity for fine structural analysis of the subendocardial conduction network. The inclusion of DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining to contextualize cellular architecture without interfering with the two primary channels. CUBIC’s compatibility with whole organs up to ~1 cm and its RI matching to ~1.49 make it ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging of intact mouse hearts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Cx40 / Hcn4 rabbit polyclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Cntn2 goat polyclonal antibody (1:150) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (10% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times, changing solution daily (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:300) and Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (1:300) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Nuclear Counterstaining  
7.1 Incubation with DAPI (10 µg/mL) in CUBIC-W (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

8 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)  
10.2 Seal chamber to prevent evaporation; image within 2 weeks using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with 488 nm and 594 nm excitation lasers.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 647, cTnT + Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of lipid-rich tissues like the mouse heart (~10 mm scale), offering rapid delipidation, excellent preservation of protein epitopes and endogenous fluorescence, and compatibility with antibody-based labeling. The method achieves high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet microscopy. For浦肯野 fiber identification, we use a dual-marker strategy: **Cx40** (highly expressed in Purkinje fibers and proximal conduction system) combined with **Hcn4** (sinoatrial/AV node marker to exclude nodal tissue) ensures specific labeling of ventricular conduction elements. **cTnT** labels cardiomyocytes to define myocardial architecture, **IB4-Lectin** highlights vasculature for spatial reference, and **DAPI** provides nuclear context—all critical for mapping Purkinje network topology relative to anatomical landmarks (endocardium, papillary muscles, apex, septum).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction; retain if strong background observed)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (vol/vol) donkey serum in PBS): anti-Cx40 (1:200), anti-Hcn4 (1:200), anti-cTnT (1:500), anti-Lectin (IB4, 10 µg/mL).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer: Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-rabbit (1:500, for Cx40/Hcn4), Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse (1:500, for cTnT), Alexa Fluor 594 streptavidin (1:500, for biotinylated IB4), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage at RT, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Prior to light-sheet or confocal imaging, equilibrate sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for ≥30 minutes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 568, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is ideal for whole mouse kidney (~10 mm scale) due to its high transparency efficiency, excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, and compatibility with nuclear and membrane protein epitopes. It enables deep imaging of intact organs without tissue shrinkage or distortion—critical for accurate 3D quantification of glomerular number, volume, and spatial distribution. The labeling strategy targets key glomerular components: Nephrin and Podocin label the slit diaphragm of podocytes to define glomerular boundaries and integrity; IB4 lectin binds endothelial glycocalyx in glomerular capillaries to visualize capillary loops; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for segmentation and cortical/medullary zoning. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series and DAPI) are well-preserved in CUBIC.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration and Delipidation (CUBIC-L)  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (10% (w/v) Triton X-100, 10% (w/v) NaOH, 25% (w/v) urea, 20% (w/v) sucrose in distilled water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L reagent. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

2 Washing  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, with 2 buffer changes)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation with anti-Nephrin (1:200), anti-Podocin (1:200), and biotinylated IB4 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Washing: Incubation with PBST. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 buffer changes every 4 hours)  
3.4 Secondary labeling: Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:400), and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  
3.5 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation with DAPI (10 µg/mL in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.6 Final wash: Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 4 buffer changes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent (50% (w/v) sucrose, 25% (w/v) urea, 10% (w/v) triethanolamine, 0.1% (w/v) Triton X-100 in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Final equilibration in CUBIC-R+ for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Store cleared kidneys in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks)  
5.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, especially for delicate subcellular structures like slit diaphragms. It is compatible with whole mouse kidneys (~10 mm scale) and allows deep, uniform antibody penetration without harsh organic solvents that could disrupt protein epitopes or fine ultrastructural context. Nephrin and Podocin are the two core transmembrane components of the slit diaphragm; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes enables precise 3D assessment of co-localization, continuity, and focal loss across all glomeruli in the intact organ. CUBIC’s RI matching to ~1.49 is ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging with standard long-working-distance objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Nephrin (1:200) and anti-Podocin (1:200) diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 12 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

3 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (3 changes, 12 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 36 hours total)  

4 CUBIC Clearing – Delipidation and Decolorization  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
4.2 Wash with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol in H₂O) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking until tissue becomes transparent)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in glass-bottom imaging chamber (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks before imaging)  
6.2 Equilibrate at RT for 1 hour prior to light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

It enables deep penetration of antibodies and compatibility with nuclear counterstains. Nephrin and Podocin are core slit diaphragm components specifically expressed in podocyte foot processes, providing precise structural delineation of the filtration barrier. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) labels glomerular endothelial luminal surfaces when perfused or incubated ex vivo, enabling 3D reconstruction of capillary loops. DAPI provides nuclear context for segmentation. CUBIC’s RI matching (~1.49) is compatible with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives (e.g., 20×/1.0 NA water-dipping), allowing whole-kidney imaging at cellular resolution.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (NPHS1, 1:200) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2, 1:200) diluted in CUBIC-B.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)

4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat wash step 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)

1 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for washing fixed kidneys. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)

(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Washing with PBST (3 changes). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, 8 hours per change)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (凝集素) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly effective aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence well, especially for large, lipid-rich organs like the mouse liver. It efficiently removes heme pigments (critical for blood-rich liver tissue) while maintaining tissue integrity at the whole-organ scale (~20 mm). CK19 is a canonical marker for biliary epithelial cells and robustly labels the entire intrahepatic bile duct tree from large ducts to small reactive ductules. Co-staining with Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* lectin) highlights portal vasculature and peribiliary vascular plexus, providing spatial reference without substituting for biliary labeling. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context. CUBIC’s high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.49) is compatible with light-sheet and confocal microscopy for volumetric imaging of complex 3D bile duct networks.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-CK19 (导管) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times with fresh CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Lectin/DAPI Co-staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat/mouse IgG (matching host of CK19 antibody) at 1:300, Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum*) at 10 µg/mL, and DAPI at 5 µg/mL, all in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
7.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.5% (wt/vol) antiphotobleaching reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate), RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at 4 ℃ in dark)  
8.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in CUBIC-R+ at RT for 24 hours to ensure uniform RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 488, CK7+Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is ideal for whole-organ clearing of lipid-rich, blood-containing tissues like mouse liver due to its strong delipidation and hemoglobin removal capabilities via amino alcohol-based reagents. It preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling of cytoskeletal and epithelial markers such as cytokeratins. Dual labeling with CK19 (canonical biliary marker) and CK7 (reactive ductular marker) enables robust cross-validation of bile duct identity, minimizing misassignment from hepatocyte cords or vasculature. IB4 lectin labels vascular endothelium to provide spatial reference for portal tracts, while DAPI offers nuclear context without interfering with biliary signal. CUBIC’s aqueous nature maintains tissue integrity and antibody penetration in ~20 mm samples, and its final RI (~1.49) matches common light-sheet objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Hemoglobin Removal & Initial Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
2.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: CUBIC-L + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CK19 (1:200), anti-CK7 (1:200) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 day, with 3 buffer changes)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rat (1:400), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-rabbit (1:400), plus Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 (1:100) and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in CUBIC-L + 5% serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
3.5 Wash with CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days, with daily buffer changes)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 30% (vol/vol) triethanolamine in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
4.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ and seal (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite storage; equilibrate to RT before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 (导管) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a high-refractive-index aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence well in large, fixed organs like the mouse liver (~20 mm scale). It enables deep, uniform penetration of antibodies into dense parenchymal tissue without requiring harsh organic solvents that may quench fluorophores. CK19 is a canonical marker for biliary epithelial cells across all ductal segments (from interlobular bile ducts to ductules), enabling full reconstruction of the bile duct tree. CD31 labels vascular endothelium, while IB4 lectin specifically binds to glycoconjugates on sinusoidal and portal vascular lumens—both serve as spatial anchors for portal tracts. DAPI provides nuclear context for assessing ductular reaction and cellular density. CUBIC’s RI matching (~1.49) is compatible with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives (e.g., 20×/1.0 NA water-dipping), allowing high-resolution 3D imaging of entire liver lobes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (blocking buffer: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-CK19 (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times with fresh CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody + Lectin + Nuclear Counterstain Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:300, for CK19), Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:300, for CD31), Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated IB4 (10 μg/mL), and DAPI (1 μg/mL) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC-L  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N,N-bis(2-hydroxyethyl)-2-aminoethanesulfonic acid, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (vol/vol) polyethylene glycol monoalkyl ether in H₂O, pH 9.0) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  
7.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19 + Alexa Fluor 488, CK7 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for dense, lipid-rich, and highly pigmented organs like the liver, offering strong decolorization via H₂O₂/methanol and effective delipidation while preserving protein epitopes and fluorescence. The original attempt used insufficient decolorization (12 h) and rapid methanol dehydration (30 min steps), leading to poor transparency and weak signal. Extending decolorization and methanol steps ensures complete hemoglobin removal and tissue permeabilization. Dual labeling with CK19 (canonical biliary marker) and CK7 (complementary ductal cytokeratin) provides comprehensive coverage of the entire bile duct tree—including small interlobular ducts (CK19⁺) and larger reactive/proliferative ductules (CK7⁺)—enabling robust 3D reconstruction of branching architecture, dilation, and network connectivity in injury models.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decolorization  
1.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes ice-cold 100% MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody penetration)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CK19 (e.g., TROMA-III, 1:200) and anti-CK7 (e.g., OV-TL 12/30, 1:150) diluted in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat washing step 3 times, changing buffer every 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Total Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
8.2 Repeat washing step 3 times, changing buffer every 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Total Time: 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A (10% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) N,N-diethylformamide, 10% (vol/vol) dichloromethane in water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-B (50% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 30% (wt/vol) N,N-diethylformamide, 20% (vol/vol) dichloromethane in water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-M (80% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 20% (wt/vol) N,N-diethylformamide, RI ≈ 1.46). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to fresh PEGASOS-M in a glass imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
12.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in PEGASOS-M, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Indefinite)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并匹配适合完整肺叶三维成像的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的 Phalloidin 可以直接提供 F-actin 结构参考，应优先作为辅助探针使用；但气道平滑肌身份仍需由表内平滑肌相关靶点完成。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, α-SMA (smooth muscle actin) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a highly effective aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence well in fixed tissues up to ~1 cm in size, making it ideal for intact mouse lung lobes (~10 mm). It provides excellent transparency while maintaining protein epitopes for antibody labeling—critical for specific identification of airway smooth muscle via α-SMA. Phalloidin robustly labels F-actin in smooth muscle and epithelial cytoskeleton, offering structural context for airway wall architecture; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue orientation. CUBIC’s RI (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives, enabling high-resolution 3D imaging of branching airways.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-α-SMA primary antibody (e.g., clone 1A4, 1:200 dilution) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin/DAPI Co-staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100), and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
8.2 Store at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ for long-term preservation (RI ≈ 1.49); image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate immersion medium matching RI = 1.49.

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 488, Desmin + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is optimized for dense, lipid-rich organs like lung and preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence better than organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), which often quench signals from cytoskeletal proteins like α-SMA and Desmin. The inclusion of a full decoloration step removes heme-derived autofluorescence that obscures deep airway imaging, while extended delipidation ensures uniform clearing of alveolar parenchyma without distorting airway architecture. Dual smooth muscle markers (α-SMA for contractile phenotype, Desmin for structural integrity) enable comprehensive assessment of remodeling across airway generations. Co-staining with IB4-Lectin highlights endothelial/vascular landmarks adjacent to airways, aiding spatial registration in 3D without interfering with smooth muscle signals. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are compatible with PEGASOS’ aqueous-organic hybrid chemistry and resist bleaching during long-term imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decoloration  
1.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Repeat 100% methanol incubation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation  
3.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Delipidation Reagent (1% (wt/vol) SDS, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.5, 1 mM EDTA, 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃) under gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Repeat delipidation with fresh reagent. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST (PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Repeat PBST wash. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.3 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Immunolabeling  
5.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) under gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

5.3 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  
5.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:300), Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:300), and Alexa Fluor 647 streptavidin (1:400) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.5 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 4 buffer changes)

6.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

7.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-RI Matching Solution A (20% (wt/vol) PEG 400, 10% (wt/vol) glycerol, 0.5% (wt/vol) urea in PBS). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin + Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, which is critical for reliable detection of β cells via insulin and PDX1 immunolabeling in the delicate, lipid-rich pancreatic tissue. It effectively clears whole mouse pancreata (~15 mm scale) without significant distortion, enabling accurate 3D quantification of dispersed islets. Insulin labels mature β cells, PDX1 marks pancreatic progenitor and β-cell nuclei (enhancing specificity and segmentation), and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture and cell counting—none of which are replaced by non-specific dyes. CUBIC’s compatibility with standard confocal and light-sheet microscopy ensures high-resolution volumetric imaging required for precise β-cell volume and spatial distribution analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Insulin (1:500), anti-PDX1 (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 6 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 18 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-guinea pig (for Insulin), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-rabbit (for PDX1), both at 1:500, plus DAPI (1 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 4 changes, 6 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

2 Dehydration (optional pre-clearing step for CUBIC to reduce processing time)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) sucrose in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2–3 days)  
3.2 Wash with PBS: 3 changes, 6 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 18 hours total)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking; replace once after 24 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched RI cuvette. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 2 weeks for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin + Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well—critical for detecting protein epitopes like Insulin and PDX1 in fixed pancreatic tissue. It effectively clears lipid-rich tissues such as the pancreas without harsh organic solvents that could denature antigens or quench fluorophores. The combination of Insulin (mature β-cell hormone product) and PDX1 (key β-cell developmental/transcription factor) provides complementary identification of functional and identity states of β-cells across all islets. DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain to delineate islet boundaries and enable accurate 3D segmentation for volumetric β-cell burden quantification. CUBIC’s compatibility with standard immunolabeling protocols and its ability to render whole mouse pancreata (~15 mm scale) transparent within days make it ideal for this application.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Insulin (e.g., guinea pig anti-Insulin, 1:500) and anti-PDX1 (e.g., rabbit anti-PDX1, 1:200) diluted in CUBIC-A (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-guinea pig IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

7 Optical Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) PVP in water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging chamber or glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
8.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ (protected from light) for up to 2 weeks without signal degradation.

**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling in thick tissues like the intact mouse pancreas (~15 mm). DAPI is included only as a nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture reference and segmentation assistance, not for β-cell quantification. CUBIC’s high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.49) is ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging of whole pancreata.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling (Perform before delipidation to preserve epitopes)  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Insulin (1:200) and anti-PDX1 (1:100) diluted in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (6 changes over 3 days, 8–12 hours per wash).(Temperature: RT, Time: total 72 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-guinea pig (for Insulin) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit (for PDX1), both at 1:300 in PBST with 5% serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
2.5 Washing with PBST (6 changes over 3 days, 8–12 hours per wash).(Temperature: RT, Time: total 72 hours)  
2.6 Optional nuclear counterstain: incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) for delipidation and initial clearing.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin + Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1 + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is a fructose-based, non-denaturing, aqueous optical clearing method that preserves protein epitopes and endogenous fluorescence with minimal tissue distortion—critical for soft, lipid-poor organs like the mouse pancreas. Unlike harsh delipidation protocols (e.g., CUBIC at 45°C for 96 h), SeeDB2 avoids high temperature and strong detergents, thereby preserving fragile islet architecture and labile hormone antigens such as insulin. It is compatible with standard immunolabeling and maintains signal intensity of Alexa Fluor dyes. The combination of Insulin (β-cell hormone product) and PDX1 (key β-cell transcription factor) enables robust dual identification of functional β-cells, while DAPI provides nuclear reference for segmentation and volume quantification in 3D.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash fixed pancreas in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
1.2 Incubation in blocking solution: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Insulin (1:500) and anti-PDX1 (1:200) diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly in PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 6 changes, 1 hour each)  
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-guinea pig (for Insulin) and Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-rabbit (for PDX1), both at 1:500 in blocking solution, plus DAPI (1 µg/mL) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.6 Wash in PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 6 changes, 1 hour each)  

2 Dehydration (optional mild dehydration to enhance RI matching)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) fructose in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) fructose in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching with SeeDB2  
3.1 Incubation with SeeDB2-S (63.4% (wt/wt) fructose, 14.2% (wt/wt) sucrose, 0.05% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with SeeDB2-F (80.2% (wt/wt) fructose, 0.05% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer cleared pancreas into fresh SeeDB2-F in glass-bottom imaging dish or matched capillary tube (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: until imaging)  
4.2 Image immediately using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for Alexa Fluor 488 (Ex/Em ~495/519 nm), Alexa Fluor 594 (Ex/Em ~590/617 nm), and DAPI (Ex/Em ~358/461 nm).

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for lipid-rich tissues like white adipose tissue (WAT), providing robust delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence. Its organic solvent–based protocol efficiently removes lipids that otherwise cause light scattering and tissue buoyancy—key challenges in WAT clearing. TH is the rate-limiting enzyme in catecholamine synthesis and a definitive marker for sympathetic nerve fibers; co-staining with CD31 delineates vasculature to analyze perivascular innervation patterns, and DAPI provides nuclear context without interfering with neural or vascular signals. Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with iDISCO+ due to their photostability and resistance to organic solvents.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction in fat)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 5 times over 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rat (1:400), plus DAPI (1:1000), diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 5 times over 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

我在进行小鼠白色脂肪组织透明化实验后发现，组织仍然不透明，并且漂浮在 RI matching 溶液表面。此前使用 PEGASOS protocol，但因为担心影响荧光而跳过了 methanol 梯度脱水步骤，直接进行了脱脂/脱色试剂和 RI matching。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合高脂肪组织的充分脱脂、渐进脱水、RI 均一匹配、交感神经双信号检测、低背景和深层三维成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。
