SCRI Renaissance 2200 is a cell wall–specific fluorescent dye that binds polysaccharides in plant cell walls and is compatible with ClearSee, providing high-contrast labeling of epidermis, cortex, endodermis, vasculature, and root meristem without antibody staining. This combination allows direct 3D correlation of transgene expression (GFP/YFP) with anatomical landmarks defined by cell wall architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if fixed in alcohol-based fixative; skip if fixed in aqueous PFA only)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

2 Post-fixation (if not already adequately fixed)  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1× PBS (pH 7.2) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Cell wall staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
3.1 Incubation with 10 µg/mL SCRI Renaissance 2200 in 1× PBS (prepared fresh from DMSO stock, final DMSO ≤0.1%) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 1× PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes, protected from light)  

4 ClearSee clearing  
4.1 Incubation with ClearSee solution (10% (wt/vol) xylitol, 10% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 25% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Replace with fresh ClearSee solution (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Optional: Replace with fresh ClearSee solution for highly pigmented samples (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with 80% (wt/vol) glycerol in distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Transfer to 100% (vol/vol) glycerol for long-term storage or immediate imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP/YFP (内源), SCRI Renaissance 2200]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is highly effective for plant tissues, offering strong delipidation and decolorization capabilities that efficiently remove chlorophyll while preserving endogenous GFP/YFP fluorescence—superior to ClearSee for pigmented samples like intact Arabidopsis seedlings. Its high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.49) aqueous reagents are compatible with hydrophilic cell wall dyes such as SCRI Renaissance 2200, which specifically labels cellulose-rich structures (cell walls, vasculature) without requiring covalent fixation or harsh permeabilization. The protocol integrates dye staining after clearing to avoid quenching and ensures deep penetration in 15–20 mm whole seedlings.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration and Chlorophyll Removal  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 CUBIC Clearing and Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Cell Wall Staining with SCRI Renaissance 2200  
3.1 Wash with CUBIC-P solution (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water) three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
3.2 Incubation with SCRI Renaissance 2200 diluted 1:200 in CUBIC-P solution (final concentration ~5 µg/mL).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.3 Wash with CUBIC-P solution three times, 2 hours each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) triethanolamine, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer samples to glass-bottom imaging dishes or capillary tubes filled with CUBIC-R+ solution for immediate imaging or short-term storage at 4 ℃ (protected from light, stable for ≥1 week).

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and labeled fluorescence exceptionally well in dense tissues like skeletal muscle, with minimal sample shrinkage or distortion—critical for accurate NMJ morphometric analysis. It effectively clears samples up to ~5–10 mm in thickness without delipidation-induced signal loss. Alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) with high affinity, enabling precise visualization of NMJ morphology; co-labeling with TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) via Alexa Fluor 488 allows simultaneous imaging of motor axon terminals to confirm synaptic apposition. CUBIC’s compatibility with protein epitopes and small-molecule probes makes it ideal for this dual-labeling strategy, and its RI (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (wt/vol) PVP, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Fluorescent Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with labeling solution containing 2 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin and 1:500 anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (3 changes, 2 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
2.3 Incubation with 1:1000 Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated secondary antibody in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  
2.4 Wash with CUBIC-B (3 changes, 2 hours each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

3 Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N,N,N’,N’-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.5) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer sample to CUBIC-R+ in glass-bottom imaging dish or matched chamber (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  
4.2 Store long-term in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark (sealed container) for up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-toxic, and highly effective clearing method for intact skeletal muscle tissue (~8 mm scale), preserving endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence while enabling deep imaging of NMJs. α-bungarotoxin specifically and covalently binds to postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) with high affinity, providing a robust, direct fluorescent signal for NMJ postsynaptic structure without requiring antibodies. TUJ1 (β-III Tubulin) is a well-established neuronal marker for motor axons and nerve terminals; combined with a bright Alexa Fluor 488 secondary, it enables precise visualization of presynaptic motor nerve endings. CUBIC’s compatibility with protein epitopes and minimal tissue shrinkage/swelling ensures accurate spatial correlation between pre- and postsynaptic components across the entire muscle volume.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling and Staining  
1.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody against β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.5 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500 in blocking solution) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated α-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.6 Wash with PBST, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Dehydration (Optional pre-CUBIC step for improved clearing kinetics in dense muscle)  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Rehydration: reverse series from 80% to 20% methanol in PBS, 30 min each (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE) in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ for final RI matching (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging dish or chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and conjugated fluorescence exceptionally well—critical for multi-color labeling of delicate structures like NMJs and axons in intact skeletal muscle. It effectively clears dense tissues such as whole mouse gastrocnemius (~8 mm scale) without causing significant shrinkage or distortion, enabling accurate 3D spatial mapping. Alpha-bungarotoxin directly and specifically labels postsynaptic AChR clusters at NMJs; Phalloidin provides high-fidelity F-actin reference of myofibers; and TUJ1 antibody labels motor axons/neurites to assess innervation coverage—all compatible with CUBIC’s mild detergent and high-sucrose environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (for β-III Tubulin)  
3.1 Incubation with anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:300 in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 12 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody + Phalloidin + alpha-bungarotoxin Co-staining  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated secondary antibody (1:500), Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200), and alpha-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor 647 (2 µg/mL) all diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  
4.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 12 hours, protected from light)  

5 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) NaN₃ in H₂O, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
5.4 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
6.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark for long-term preservation; equilibrate to RT before imaging.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin–Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that minimizes tissue shrinkage and preserves protein epitopes and fluorescent signals—critical for maintaining the delicate architecture of NMJs and robust alpha-bungarotoxin binding to AChRs. Unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO), CUBIC avoids severe dehydration-induced muscle contraction and preserves the native morphology of skeletal muscle fibers. It also supports effective immunolabeling of intracellular targets like β-III tubulin in motor axons without requiring harsh permeabilization. The combination of directly conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (for postsynaptic AChR clusters) and anti–β-III tubulin antibody (for presynaptic axonal cytoskeleton) enables high-fidelity 3D visualization of NMJ pairing, fragmentation, and denervation. CUBIC’s refractive index (~1.49) is compatible with standard confocal and light-sheet objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or dehydrated)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 solution (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B solution (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (for β-III Tubulin)  
3.1 Incubation with anti–β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) primary antibody diluted 1:500 in CUBIC-B.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (3 changes, 2 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody and Alpha-Bungarotoxin Co-Staining  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1 µg/mL) in CUBIC-B.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

5 Post-Staining Washes  
5.1 Wash with CUBIC-B (3 changes, 4 hours each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
5.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

6 Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
7.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dish or chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
7.2 Store at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ with 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide for long-term preservation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.49) clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well in thick, lipid-rich tissues like the mouse stomach. It effectively clears multi-layered organs while maintaining fine neural structures. PGP9.5 (also known as UCHL1) is a pan-neuronal cytoplasmic marker that robustly labels all enteric and extrinsic nerve fibers—including main trunks, branches, and terminal arborizations—throughout the entire gastric wall, fulfilling the requirement for comprehensive neural network visualization. Alexa Fluor 647 provides far-red emission compatible with CUBIC’s low autofluorescence in this channel and enables deep-tissue imaging. DAPI counterstains nuclei to aid layer identification (mucosa vs. muscle vs. serosa). CUBIC’s gentle delipidation and RI matching are ideal for preserving the 3D architecture of the ~8 mm-thick stomach without shrinkage or distortion, enabling accurate spatial mapping across gastric regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-40), 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) PVP-40, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (e.g., Abcam ab108986 or equivalent, diluted 1:500 in CUBIC-B + 5% NDS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (or appropriate host-matched secondary, diluted 1:500 in CUBIC-B + 5% NDS) and DAPI (1 µg/mL) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-Staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.

PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker recognizing ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1) and HuC/D (RNA-binding proteins specific to neuronal cell bodies and processes) provide complementary labeling of the entire enteric and extrinsic innervation network across all gastric wall layers. Alexa Fluor 647 and 488 offer photostable, spectrally distinct signals suitable for multichannel light-sheet imaging. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture reference without interfering with neural channels.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.49) clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence well, is compatible with whole-organ clearing of moderately sized tissues like the mouse stomach (~20 mm), and allows deep penetration of large probes such as antibodies and phalloidin conjugates. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) robustly labels all enteric and vagal nerve fibers and terminals throughout the gastric wall, while Phalloidin specifically labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers (circular and longitudinal), providing essential structural reference for spatial mapping of neural architecture relative to motility-related musculature. CUBIC’s gentle delipidation and minimal tissue shrinkage preserve 3D morphology critical for accurate spatial correlation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (1:500 dilution in CUBIC-B) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC-L  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥4 weeks)  
9.2 Mount in CUBIC-R+ within a custom chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of lipid-rich tissues like the stomach, offering deep antibody penetration, strong autofluorescence quenching, and excellent preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes. The methanol-based dehydration and delipidation steps effectively reduce background while enhancing antibody access to dense gastric wall layers. PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) labels all nerve fibers including vagal terminals, while TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) specifically marks catecholaminergic vagal efferents—enabling dual-channel mapping of total vs. functional vagal innervation across mucosa, submucosa, muscularis, and serosa. This combination avoids reliance on weak endogenous fluorescence and leverages robust, validated primary antibodies with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor secondaries compatible with iDISCO+.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching / Autofluorescence Quenching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared by mixing 1 volume 30% H₂O₂ with 5 volumes methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (post-bleach)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization & Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibody mix: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and anti-TH (1:300) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (vol/vol) donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Washing (Primary Removal)  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer A (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibody mix: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (same as 5.1) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, with gentle shaking)  

8 Washing (Secondary Removal)  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer A (same as 6.1) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  
8.3 Final rinse with 100% PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Repeat step 9.5 once (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer to fresh 100% DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

12.1 Store cleared stomach in sealed DBE-filled glass vial at RT, protected from light. Image within 1 week using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with 488 nm and 594 nm laser lines.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP, tdTomato, MAP2]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., EGFP and tdTomato), which are critical for tracing long-range projections from amygdala, prefrontal cortex, thalamus, and nucleus accumbens. It provides strong delipidation and high transparency while maintaining signal integrity over weeks. To visualize local dendritic arborization and neuronal morphology in target regions, we immunolabel for MAP2—a well-established marker of dendritic cytoskeleton—using a primary antibody followed by an Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary compatible with iDISCO+ organic solvents. This combination enables simultaneous mapping of projection pathways (via endogenous reporters) and local dendritic architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous fluorescence protection (optional but recommended for EGFP/tdTomato)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary antibody labeling (anti-MAP2)  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing anti-MAP2 primary antibody (e.g., mouse anti-MAP2, 1:500 dilution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary antibody labeling  
7.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:500 dilution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunolabeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Repeat step 10.1 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive index matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

12 Storage and imaging preparation  
12.1 Store cleared brain in DBE at RT in the dark for up to 2 weeks; image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate excitation/emission filters for EGFP (~488/510 nm), tdTomato (~554/581 nm), and Alexa Fluor 647 (~650/668 nm).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (activity-dependent neuronal marker) + Alexa Fluor 647, NeuN + Alexa Fluor 488, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires mapping activity-dependent neuronal ensembles across the entire brain and preserving the spatial relationship between the tongue and brainstem nuclei involved in arousal and motor control. c-Fos is a well-established immediate-early gene marker for neuronal activation during behavioral tasks like anesthesia recovery. To distinguish activated neurons from total neurons and label peripheral innervation in the tongue, we combine c-Fos immunolabeling with NeuN (pan-neuronal nuclear marker) and IB4 (labels sensory nerve endings and vasculature in tongue). iDISCO+ is selected because it efficiently clears large, lipid-rich tissues like whole mouse brain and tongue while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, especially for far-red and near-infrared fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor 647), which suffer less from autofluorescence and scattering. Its organic solvent–based dehydration and delipidation steps are compatible with fixed, post-fixed samples and provide excellent refractive index matching for light-sheet imaging of intact brain-tongue specimens.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for reducing autofluorescence in tongue and brainstem)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum: anti-c-Fos (1:500), anti-NeuN (1:500), anti-IB4 (biotinylated, 1:200).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes every 4 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum: Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit (1:500, for c-Fos), Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (1:500, for NeuN), Streptavidin-Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500, for IB4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes every 4 hours, protected from light)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-c-Fos (rabbit, 1:500) and anti-Npas4 (goat, 1:300) in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash

9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

*Note: DAPI was included in labeling strategy but applied during rehydration step if needed; however, for iDISCO+, nuclear dyes are best applied before dehydration. If omitted earlier, skip this step as DAPI does not penetrate well post-DCM/DBE.*

13.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with fresh DBE, sealed to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (IEG marker for activated neurons) + Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated secondary antibody, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (for tongue F-actin/muscle architecture), DAPI (nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference)]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-mount immunolabeling of large, lipid-rich tissues like the intact mouse brain and tongue. It enables deep penetration of antibodies against immediate early genes (e.g., c-Fos) while preserving endogenous fluorescence and providing excellent clearing for light-sheet imaging. The methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM)/dibenzyl ether (DBE) refractive index matching yield high transparency and compatibility with lipophilic dyes. Phalloidin labels F-actin in tongue musculature to delineate effector anatomy, and DAPI provides nuclear landmarks for registration—both are compatible with iDISCO+’s organic solvent workflow. c-Fos immunostaining reliably identifies neurons activated during anesthesia-awakening transitions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The problem requires tracing two distinct lipophilic neuronal projections across large, lipid-rich CNS tissues (spinal cord, thalamus, somatosensory cortex). DiI and DiD are ideal for long-range axonal tracing due to their stable membrane integration, minimal diffusion, and spectrally separable emission (DiI: ~565 nm; DiD: ~665 nm). iDISCO+ is selected because it is a methanol- and dichloromethane (DCM)-based organic solvent clearing method that efficiently delipidates dense neural tissue while preserving lipophilic dye fluorescence—unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) which often quench or extract DiI/DiD. iDISCO+ also achieves high transparency in thick samples (up to whole mouse brain) and matches refractive index with dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56), compatible with light-sheet microscopy for 3D circuit mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for background reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 0.2% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 0.2% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Dehydration (second round)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Dichloromethane (DCM) Treatment  
6.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE in glass vial, protected from light.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12–24 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Store cleared samples immersed in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite, up to 1 month)  
8.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a highly effective organic solvent–based clearing method optimized for whole-mount immunolabeling and lipophilic dye preservation in large neural tissues such as spinal cord and brain. It provides excellent delipidation and refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.56) compatible with light-sheet microscopy, while robustly preserving the fluorescence of carbocyanine dyes like DiI and DiD—ideal for long-range axonal tracing. TO-PRO-3 is included as a nuclear counterstain to enable anatomical registration of thalamic nuclei and cortical layers without interfering with DiI/DiD signals (emission spectra well-separated). This combination allows precise 3D mapping of dual sensory pathways from spinal entry to thalamocortical termination zones.

**Protocol Steps:**

3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation

我在进行小鼠脊髓-丘脑-皮层感觉通路透明化实验时遇到问题：固定后直接放入 SDS 清除液中处理 48 小时，然后进行 Alexa Fluor 647 孵育 24 小时，最后放入甘油中。结果组织仍然不透明，且 Alexa Fluor 647 信号分布不均匀。该流程与科学目标不匹配，因为目标是保留并成像 DiI/DiD 脂溶性示踪信号，而不是依赖 Alexa Fluor 抗体孵育；同时 SDS 48 小时和甘油匹配不足以完成长脊髓和脑区组织的均一透明化。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合 DiI/DiD 脂溶性示踪信号保留、长程感觉通路成像、脊髓和脑区组织充分脱水/脱脂、低背景、均一 RI 匹配和三维重建。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is a methanol- and dichloromethane (DCM)-based organic solvent clearing method optimized for whole-mount immunolabeling and endogenous fluorophore preservation in large tissues. Crucially, it is highly compatible with lipophilic carbocyanine dyes such as DiI and DiD, which partition into lipid membranes and remain stable through dehydration and delipidation steps when handled correctly. Unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS), iDISCO+ achieves deep, uniform clearing in dense neural tissues like spinal cord and thalamus by aggressive delipidation, enabling homogeneous refractive index (RI) matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56). The protocol includes controlled rehydration before dye application to allow diffusion, followed by gradual dehydration to lock dyes in place—critical for preserving long-range axonal tracing signals across the 3 cm spinal cord–thalamus–cortex axis. This approach avoids antibody-based labeling (unnecessary here) and ensures low background, high signal retention, and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy for 3D reconstruction of overlapping/parallel somatosensory pathways.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (for DiI/DiD labeling)  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 10% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Lipophilic Tracer Labeling  
2.1 Incubation with DiI (2 µg/µL in DMSO) and DiD (2 µg/µL in DMSO) diluted 1:100 in PBS, applied via pressure injection or direct incubation at tracer sites (e.g., dorsal root entry zone for spinal input; alternate tracers in left/right sides or distinct peripheral nerves).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Post-labeling wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Delipidation  
4.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

5 Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) DCM : dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 100% DBE (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Store samples immersed in 100% DBE in glass vials protected from light at RT.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite until imaging)  
6.2 Mount in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy; avoid air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate prior to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for lipid-rich tissues like white adipose tissue (WAT), providing strong delipidation and excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence signals. It enables deep penetration of antibodies into dense scWAT and achieves high transparency with refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) specifically labels peptidergic sensory nerve fibers; PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) provides a comprehensive neural scaffold for spatial context; and IB4 (isolectin B4 from Griffonia simplicifolia) binds to endothelial glycans in mouse vasculature, enabling clear delineation of blood vessel lumens without requiring transgenic reporters. All three targets are compatible with organic solvent–based clearing like iDISCO+, and Alexa Fluor dyes offer high photostability and minimal quenching during dehydration and delipidation steps.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Peroxidase Quenching (optional but recommended for antibody penetration)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration

3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

8.2 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Repeat PBT wash.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.4 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for lipid-rich tissues like subcutaneous white adipose tissue (scWAT) due to its strong organic solvent–based delipidation and dehydration steps, which overcome the poor clearing observed with aqueous CUBIC protocols. It preserves endogenous fluorescence poorly but is ideal for immunolabeling with Alexa Fluor dyes, which are stable in methanol and organic solvents. The combination of CGRP (sensory nerve marker), PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker), and IB4 lectin (labels vasculature and some sensory fibers) enables precise spatial mapping of nerve–vascular relationships in fat lobules, margins, and perivascular zones. RI matching with dichloromethane (DCM) and dibenzyl ether (DBE) provides high transparency and compatibility with light-sheet or confocal deep imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction in scWAT)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CGRP (1:200) + anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 changes)  

7 Secondary Antibody + Lectin Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) + Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBT + 5% NGS + 0.2% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day, with 6 changes)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DBE (dibenzyl ether, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging  
12.1 Store sample in DBE at RT in the dark until imaging. Mount in glass-bottom dish filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56).

It outperforms other methods (e.g., iDISCO+, CUBIC) in clearing dense bone with intact neural structures. The labeling strategy uses two pan-neuronal markers—β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) for axons and PGP9.5 (a ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase highly expressed in all neurons)—conjugated to spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes for robust, specific visualization of neural fibers throughout bone microenvironments. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical context. This combination ensures unambiguous identification of neural identity (not just tracer paths) within complex bony niches including cranial sutures, marrow cavities, and meningeal interfaces.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification & Initial Fixation Stabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, in PBS) containing 4% (wt/vol) PFA and 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation; change solution every 2 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)

3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

5 Wash

6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle rotation; protect from light)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 4 changes)  

8 Dehydration  
8.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

8.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues such as bone and preserves endogenous fluorescence while enabling deep immunolabeling in hard tissues like mouse skull and femur. It effectively clears both cortical bone and marrow while maintaining structural integrity of neural fibers and meninges. CGRP is the gold-standard marker for peptidergic nociceptive sensory nerve fibers; PGP9.5 (HuC/D) serves as a pan-neuronal marker to visualize the entire neural network. IB4 (Lectin) labels non-peptidergic sensory fibers and vasculature, providing complementary neural and vascular context. DAPI offers nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture without interfering with bone autofluorescence. PEGASOS’ EDTA-based decalcification integrated into clearing enables simultaneous demineralization and transparency, critical for imaging neural projections through dense bone.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Repeat incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Decalcification (PEGASOS Clearing Solution A)  
2.1 Incubation with PEGASOS Solution A (5% (wt/vol) PEG-4000, 5% (wt/vol) SDS, 20 mM EDTA, 0.2 M NaCl, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2 days)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash with PBST (PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Repeat wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunolabeling  
4.1 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with blocking buffer (PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Primary antibody incubation: Anti-CGRP (1:500) + Anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 2% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 3 days)  
4.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, change buffer every 2 hours)  
4.4 Secondary antibody + Lectin incubation: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking; protect from light)  
4.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, change buffer every 2 hours)  
4.6 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protect from light)  
4.7 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Refractive Index Matching (PEGASOS Solution B)  
5.1 Incubation with PEGASOS Solution B (50% (wt/vol) PEG-4000, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.01% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh PEGASOS Solution B.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with PEGASOS Solution B for long-term storage at 4 ℃ (protect from light).  
6.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate samples in fresh PEGASOS Solution B for 2 hours at RT.  
6.3 Mount samples in PEGASOS Solution B-compatible imaging chambers for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues including bone and calcified samples, combining efficient decalcification with high fluorescence preservation—critical for detecting delicate CGRP+ sensory fibers in dense bone. It enables uniform antibody penetration into marrow and meninges while maintaining structural integrity of vascular lumens and neural processes. The labeling strategy uses CGRP to identify sensory nerve fibers, CD31 and IB4 lectin to co-label vascular endothelium and lumen (IB4 binds glycoconjugates on endothelial surfaces), and DAPI for nuclear counterstain to delineate tissue architecture. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of neurovascular relationships within bone channels, marrow cavities, and meningeal interfaces.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Mild Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in PBS, pH 7.4, supplemented with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation; change solution every 2 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Blocking and Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 3 changes, total 36 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rat (1:400), plus IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 (10 µg/mL), all in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 3 changes)  
6.2 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

7 Dehydration  
7.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

8 Delipidation and Initial Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A solution (10% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-B solution (80% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  

10 Final Equilibration and Storage  
10.1 Incubation with fresh PEGASOS-B solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
10.2 Store samples in PEGASOS-B at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. Samples are compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

Dual labeling with CGRP (sensory fibers) and pan-neuronal marker PGP9.5 enables specific mapping of sensory vs. total innervation across bone–meningeal interfaces. Alexa Fluor 568/647 are compatible with PEGASOS’ organic solvent-based protocol and resist bleaching during delipidation.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification & Rehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, in PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Wash with PBS three times, 1 hour each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Permeabilization & Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS) six times, 6 hours each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
4.2 Wash with PBST six times, 6 hours each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours per wash)

5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
5.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 594, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard, calcified tissues such as mouse bone, enabling efficient decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunoreactivity. It allows deep penetration of antibodies into intact bone marrow cavities—critical for labeling sparse sympathetic nerve fibers (marked by TH and NPY) and vascular structures (CD31). The combination of TH (rate-limiting enzyme in norepinephrine synthesis) and NPY (co-transmitter in sympathetic fibers) provides robust identification of noradrenergic and peptidergic sympathetic innervation. CD31 delineates vasculature for spatial reference, and DAPI labels nuclei to identify hematopoietic cell-rich regions. PEGASOS maintains signal integrity of Alexa Fluor dyes and supports high-resolution 3D imaging of bone marrow microarchitecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, 20% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2 days)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200), anti-NPY (1:200), anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, change buffer daily)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–donkey anti-rabbit (1:300), Alexa Fluor 594–donkey anti-guinea pig (1:300), Alexa Fluor 647–donkey anti-rat (1:300), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking, protected from light)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 24 hours, change buffer daily, protected from light)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)  

4 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Clearing Solution A (50% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
4.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-Clearing Solution B (80% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 20% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine in water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  
4.3 Incubation with PEGASOS-Mounting Solution (90% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 30% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer samples to fresh PEGASOS-Mounting Solution in glass-bottom imaging chambers (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: store indefinitely, protected from light)  
5.2 Equilibrate at RT for 2 hours before light-sheet or confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (酪氨酸羟化酶) + Alexa Fluor 488, VIP + Alexa Fluor 594, CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues such as mouse long bones and skull, enabling efficient decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunoreactivity. It allows deep penetration of antibodies into the bone marrow cavity—critical for labeling intramedullary sympathetic nerve fibers. TH is the rate-limiting enzyme in catecholamine synthesis and serves as a canonical marker for catecholaminergic sympathetic neurons; VIP labels peptidergic sympathetic (and some parasympathetic) fibers, enabling direct comparison of the two subtypes. CD31 provides high-contrast vascular reference for spatial analysis relative to nerves, and DAPI outlines cellular/nuclear architecture without interfering with protein epitopes. BoneClear’s EDTA-based decalcification preserves protein structure better than strong acid methods, ensuring reliable antibody binding to TH and VIP.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with BoneClear-Decalc (0.5 M EDTA, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, pH 7.4 adjusted with NaOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation; replace solution every 2 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with BoneClear-Block (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200), anti-VIP (1:150), anti-CD31 (1:100) in BoneClear-Block (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replenish antibody solution every 3 days)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 4 changes)  

6 Secondary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit (1:300), Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-goat (1:300), Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-rat (1:300), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL) in BoneClear-Block (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking; protect from light)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours × 4 changes; protect from light)  

8 Dehydration  
8.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with BoneClear-RI (64% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.46) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

10 Final Equilibration and Storage  
10.1 Transfer samples to fresh BoneClear-RI in imaging-compatible glass vials (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging; store at 4 ℃ protected from light for up to 4 weeks)

**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, NPY + Alexa Fluor 594, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized bone tissues, combining efficient decalcification with gentle delipidation and refractive index matching that preserves endogenous fluorescence and enables deep antibody penetration into bone marrow cavities. Unlike SWITCH—which relies on hydrogel embedding incompatible with dense mineralized matrix—BoneClear uses EDTA-based decalcification followed by aminoalcohol-based clearing (e.g., TDE/urea), which maintains bone microarchitecture and supports robust immunolabeling of fragile catecholaminergic (TH) and peptidergic (NPY) nerve fibers. The chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are highly photostable, compatible with BoneClear’s aqueous-to-moderate-RI transition, and spectrally separable in far-red to green channels for multiplexed 3D imaging of sympathetic innervation relative to vascular (CD31) and nuclear (DAPI) landmarks.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, adjusted with NaOH) in PBS containing 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days with daily solution change)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  

3 Permeabilization and Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer: PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer: anti-TH (1:200), anti-NPY (1:100), anti-CD31 (1:100).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  

6 Secondary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-rabbit, 1:400), Alexa Fluor 594 (anti-guinea pig or appropriate host, 1:400), Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-rat, 1:400), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  

8 Dehydration  
8.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)
