**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647, Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for fixed, lipid-rich tissues like pancreatic tumors (~1 cm scale), offering deep clearing with excellent preservation of protein epitopes and fluorophores after methanol dehydration. It enables robust immunolabeling in thick samples and achieves high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.56) compatible with light-sheet microscopy. The labeling strategy combines β-III Tubulin (TUJ1)—a pan-neuronal marker labeling axons and nerve fibers—with Pan-Cytokeratin to delineate tumor epithelial boundaries, enabling precise 3D mapping of perineural invasion (PNI). DAPI provides nuclear context for tissue architecture. This combination directly addresses the need to visualize neural-tumor spatial relationships in complex stroma.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for endogenous fluorescence reduction; retain if autofluorescence interferes)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:300) diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1:1000), all diluted in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Transfer to fresh DBE for long-term storage or immediate imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 594, CK19 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimal for fixed, lipid-rich tissues like pancreatic tumors due to its strong delipidation (via methanol and DCM) and effective decolorization (H₂O₂ step), which reduces autofluorescence and enhances signal-to-noise—critical for weak neural signals and unclear tumor boundaries. It preserves Alexa Fluor dyes well and enables deep antibody penetration in samples up to ~15 mm. PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker) and TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, sympathetic-specific) provide the required dual neural labeling. CK19 labels pancreatic ductal/epithelial tumor cells to define tumor boundaries and enable precise PNI assessment. DAPI provides nuclear context without interfering with far-red channels. This combination avoids introducing non-listed targets while enabling 3D mapping of nerves relative to tumor architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Decolorization  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum: anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), anti-TH (1:500), anti-CK19 (1:300).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit/mouse (1:500), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-goat/rabbit (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse/rat (1:500), plus DAPI (1:1000).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking, protected from light)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-staining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample in glass vial filled with DBE at RT, protected from light, until imaging by light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for fixed, immunolabeled mouse brain tissue up to ~1 cm in size, offering excellent lipid removal, strong autofluorescence quenching, and high compatibility with antibody-based labeling and lectin perfusion markers. It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes well and achieves high transparency with refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet microscopy. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) injected intravascularly prior to fixation labels only perfused (functional) vasculature, while CD31 immunostaining reveals the entire endothelial network—including non-perfused or collapsed vessels—enabling direct comparison of functional vs. structural vasculature across tumor core, invasive margin, and normal parenchyma. DAPI provides nuclear context for spatial registration.

**Protocol Steps:**

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is optimal for fixed mouse brain tumor tissue (~8 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation and high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.56), enabling deep imaging of vascular networks with low background. It preserves protein epitopes better than FDISCO when proper rehydration and antibody incubation steps are included, which is critical for CD31 labeling of endothelial cells. Lectin perfusion (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) binds specifically to glycoproteins on the luminal surface of perfused vessels, allowing functional perfusion status assessment. Combining Lectin-AF647 (perfused lumen) with CD31-AF594 (total endothelium) enables quantification of perfusion fraction, vessel continuity, and heterogeneity between tumor core and margin. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial context without interfering with red/NIR channels. The original FDISCO failure (incomplete dehydration, skipped DCM) caused uneven clearing; iDISCO+’s rigorous THF/DCM dehydration-delipidation sequence resolves this.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation  
2.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.6 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Blocking and Permeabilization  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with rat anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBT + 5% serum + 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five more times (total 6 washes, each 1 hour).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 594 diluted 1:400 in PBT + 5% serum + 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days)  

8 Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five more times (total 6 washes, each 1 hour).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Nuclear Counterstain and Lectin Labeling  
9.1 Incubation with PBT containing 10 µg/mL DAPI and 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

10 Final Washing  
10.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Bleaching (optional, if autofluorescence high)  
12.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

13 Final Dehydration  
13.1 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

14 Refractive Index Matching  
14.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
14.2 Incubation with 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
14.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-organic solvent clearing method that excels at preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins like tdTomato/RFP while enabling deep antibody penetration in whole mouse brains. It is particularly suitable for samples ~1 cm in size and compatible with both intrinsic fluorescence and immunolabeling of protein epitopes such as epithelial markers. Pan-Cytokeratin robustly labels epithelial-derived tumor cells (including breast cancer metastases) and, when conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, provides a far-red channel that minimizes spectral overlap with tdTomato and avoids quenching during CUBIC processing. This dual-channel strategy allows unambiguous identification of single metastatic cells (via tdTomato) and confirmation of their epithelial identity (via Pan-Cytokeratin), fulfilling the scientific goal without relying on nuclear or vascular markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Endogenous Fluorescence Protection and Permeabilization  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N,N,N′,N′-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (THP), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: CUBIC-L + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody: Pan-Cytokeratin (e.g., mouse anti-Pan-CK, 1:200 dilution) in CUBIC-L + 5% serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
3.3 Washing with CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-mouse IgG (1:300 dilution) in CUBIC-L + 5% serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking)  
3.5 Washing with CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  

4 Optical Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 0.1% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Transfer tissue into imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ in light-protected container (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks without significant signal loss)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato/RFP (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin + Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole mouse brain clearing with excellent preservation of red fluorescent proteins like tdTomato/RFP, which is critical for tracking endogenously labeled breast cancer brain metastases. Its organic solvent–based protocol efficiently clears lipid-rich brain tissue while maintaining structural integrity and enabling deep imaging of metastatic foci. The inclusion of Pan-Cytokeratin (epithelial tumor marker) validates the carcinoma identity of tdTomato+ cells; CD31 labels vasculature to assess perivascular invasion patterns; DAPI provides nuclear context for spatial mapping. iDISCO+ also supports antibody penetration in intact brains without hydrogel embedding, making it suitable for multi-channel immunolabeling in fixed samples.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction; skip if tdTomato signal is strong and background low)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: Pan-Cytokeratin (1:200) and CD31 (1:100) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

6 Washes after Primary Antibody  
6.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse IgG (1:400) for Pan-Cytokeratin and Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rat IgG (1:400) for CD31, diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

8 Washes after Secondary Antibody  
8.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 three more times, changing solution every 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours or until imaging)  

12 Nuclear Counterstain (optional post-clearing DAPI if not done earlier; note: DAPI fluorescence may quench in DBE—perform before final DBE if needed)  
12.1 If DAPI not included during rehydration/blocking, incubate in PBST + 1 µg/mL DAPI during step 3.5 or 4.2.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours) — *Note: DAPI signal is best preserved if applied before dehydration steps 9–10; otherwise omit as tdTomato/Pan-CK/CD31 suffice for core goals.*

CUBIC induces minimal tissue deformation (<5% linear shrinkage), crucial for accurate 3D mapping of invasion fronts. It is compatible with immunolabeling of nuclear and cytoplasmic epitopes such as Pan-Cytokeratin, enabling specific identification of epithelial-derived metastatic cells within brain parenchyma. The protocol avoids harsh dehydration or delipidation steps that degrade RFP signals and instead uses gentle amino alcohol–based reagents (CUBIC-L and CUBIC-R+) that maintain protein conformation and fluorescence.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, with 2 buffer changes)

2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10 wt% Quadrol, 10 wt% urea, 5 vol% Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6 Secondary Antibody Wash

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, TH + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for mineralized hard tissues such as bone, integrating efficient decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching in a single workflow while preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration. It outperforms aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS) in clearing dense cortical bone and maintains protein epitopes better than organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+, uDISCO) for immunolabeling of neuropeptides like CGRP and TH. The chosen labeling uses primary antibodies against CGRP (sensory marker) and TH (sympathetic marker), conjugated to spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes for high-sensitivity, specific detection in 3D; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical reference without interfering with neural signals.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, 20% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2 days)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Wash with PBT (PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-TH (1:500) diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  
2.4 Wash with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes, 3 hours per change)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:800) and Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking, protected from light)  
2.6 Wash with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours × 4 changes, 3 hours per change, protected from light)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 2 changes)  

4 Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-Clearing Solution A (50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane, 50% (vol/vol) methanol) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PEGASOS-Clearing Solution B (100% dichloromethane) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 2 changes)  
4.3 Incubation with PEGASOS-Matching Solution (benzyl alcohol : benzyl benzoate = 1:2 (vol/vol), RI ≈ 1.56) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer sample into fresh PEGASOS-Matching Solution in glass vial (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite storage at RT, protected from light)  
5.2 Mount sample in imaging chamber filled with PEGASOS-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues like mouse bone, enabling efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes. It achieves high transparency in dense cortical and trabecular bone without requiring harsh organic solvents that quench fluorophores. The labeling strategy uses CGRP (calcitonin gene-related peptide) as the specific marker for peptidergic nociceptive fibers, PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) to visualize the entire intraosseous nerve network, IB4-Lectin to label non-peptidergic sensory fibers and vasculature (as a structural reference), and DAPI for nuclear counterstain to delineate bone marrow cellular zones. Alexa Fluor dyes are chosen for their photostability and compatibility with BoneClear’s aqueous-based protocol.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation and Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for re-fixation if needed.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with BoneClear Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, pH 7.4, 0.1% NaN₃).(Temperature: RT with gentle shaking, Time: 7–10 days, until softening confirmed by needle test)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with BoneClear Permeabilization Buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with BoneClear Blocking Buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CGRP (1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:1000) diluted in BoneClear Antibody Dilution Buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, 0.02% NaN₃ in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃ with gentle shaking, Time: 7 days)  
3.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 24 hours, with buffer changes every 24 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) for CGRP, Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse (1:500) for PGP9.5, and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL), all diluted in BoneClear Antibody Dilution Buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃ in dark with gentle shaking, Time: 5 days)  
4.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT in dark, Time: 5 × 24 hours, with buffer changes every 24 hours)  

5 Nuclear Counterstaining  
5.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBST).(Temperature: RT in dark, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT in dark, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  

6 Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI Matching Solution A (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.42).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with BoneClear RI Matching Solution B (70% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% Triton X-100, RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with BoneClear Final Clearing Solution (85% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% Triton X-100, RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer samples into glass vials filled with BoneClear Final Clearing Solution supplemented with 0.02% sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃ in dark, long-term storage)  
7.2 Mount cleared femurs vertically in imaging chambers using 1.5% low-melting agarose in BoneClear Final Clearing Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging after solidification)

The use of Alexa Fluor conjugates ensures bright, photostable signals compatible with light-sheet or confocal 3D imaging of dense bone matrices. This strategy enables simultaneous visualization of sensory (CGRP⁺), sympathetic (TH⁺), and total (PGP9.5⁺) nerve fibers in bone marrow, endosteum, periosteum, and tumor-adjacent regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, adjusted with NaOH) containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with daily solution replacement)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, with 3 changes every 30 min)

3.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A (20% (wt/vol) polyethylene glycol 400, 10% (wt/vol) N-methylglucamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, with gentle shaking)

6.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-rabbit), Alexa Fluor 594 (anti-goat), and Alexa Fluor 647 (anti-mouse), each at 1:300 dilution in PEGASOS-B.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light, with gentle shaking)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PEGASOS-B without antibodies.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days, with 4 buffer changes every 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for E9.5–E10.5 mouse embryo trunk samples (~5 mm scale) due to its rapid, organic solvent–based delipidation and strong compatibility with endogenous red fluorescent proteins like tdTomato, which are otherwise prone to quenching in aqueous clearing methods. It also enables robust immunolabeling of nuclear transcription factors such as Sox10—a key marker for neural crest and glial lineage identity—using methanol-compatible primary/secondary antibodies. The method achieves high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for light-sheet or confocal imaging of 3D migration paths from dorsal neural tube to peripheral targets (DRG, sympathetic chain).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for endogenous fluorescence preservation; skip if tdTomato signal is strong and background low)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining (Sox10)  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Sox10 primary antibody (e.g., R&D Systems AF2864 or equivalent) diluted 1:200 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing solution every 1–2 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (or appropriate host-matched secondary) diluted 1:400 in PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times over 12 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: total 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite until imaging)  
12.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D acquisition of tdTomato (neural crest lineage) and Alexa Fluor 647 (Sox10⁺ cells).

我在进行小鼠胚胎神经嵴细胞透明化实验后发现，神经嵴细胞标记信号不均匀，胚胎中心区域信号弱，且组织结构有破坏。此前使用 ClearT2 protocol，但又加入了每步仅 30 分钟的 methanol gradient 和 4 小时 decoloration，可能造成胚胎组织渗透不充分、信号进入不足，同时因脱水/脱色处理不当导致 tdTomato 衰减和组织损伤。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合胚胎小组织块的低形变处理、tdTomato 内源信号保留、Sox10 抗体深层渗透、低背景和三维迁移路径成像。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-organic solvent clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence (especially red fluorophores like tdTomato) far better than methanol-heavy protocols such as iDISCO+ or ClearT2. It enables deep antibody penetration in small embryonic tissues without significant tissue shrinkage or structural distortion—critical for preserving the delicate morphology of E9.5–E10.5 mouse embryo trunk and accurate 3D reconstruction of neural crest migration paths. The high refractive index (~1.49) of CUBIC reagents matches well with light-sheet microscopy, and its mild delipidation preserves epitopes for nuclear transcription factors like Sox10. Avoiding methanol gradients and harsh decolorization prevents tdTomato quenching and tissue damage observed in prior attempts.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if previously dehydrated)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Sox10 primary antibody (e.g., rabbit anti-Sox10, 1:200 dilution in CUBIC-B) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:300 dilution in CUBIC-B) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.5% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in H₂O; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ and seal (Temperature: 4 ℃ for storage; RT for imaging) (Time: store up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), IB4 (Alexa Fluor 594 conjugate), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a high-refractive-index aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence exceptionally well in lipid-rich, moderately sized tissues like the mouse placenta (~10–12 mm). It enables deep penetration of large molecular probes (e.g., antibodies) and is compatible with lectin/IB4 perfusion labeling of functional vascular lumens. The combination of intravascular Lectin/IB4 (which bind endothelial glycocalyx only in perfused vessels) with CD31 immunostaining allows discrimination between structurally present vs. functionally perfused vasculature. CUBIC’s RI (~1.49) matches well with light-sheet microscopy objectives and causes minimal tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D morphometric analysis of delicate labyrinthine villous trees.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion-Based Vascular Lumen Labeling (performed prior to fixation if possible; if post-fixed, proceed with passive incubation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin and 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4 in PBS containing 1 mM CaCl₂ and 1 mM MnCl₂ to support lectin binding. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.2 Wash with PBS + 1 mM CaCl₂/MnCl₂. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 Post-Fixation (if not already fully fixed)  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling for CD31 and Nuclear Counterstain  
3.1 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Blocking with CUBIC-Ab solution (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-40), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with rat anti-mouse CD31 primary antibody (1:200 dilution) in CUBIC-Ab solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
3.4 Wash with CUBIC-Ab solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  
3.5 Incubation with goat anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody (1:500 dilution) + 5 µg/mL DAPI in CUBIC-Ab solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.6 Wash with CUBIC-Ab solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 24 hours)  

4 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N,N,N’,N’-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine (Quadrol), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 5% (wt/vol) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2–3 days)  
4.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  
4.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2’-thiodiethanol (TDE) in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.49). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace once at day 4)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Final equilibration in fresh CUBIC-R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Store and image samples immersed in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in light-protected containers. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks for optimal signal stability)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647), CD31 (PECAM1) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is highly effective for lipid-rich, blood-containing tissues like mouse placenta due to its strong delipidation and hemoglobin removal steps, which drastically reduce background autofluorescence. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) binds specifically to endothelial glycocalyx and labels functional perfused vasculature when injected pre-fixation; CD31 antibody labels all endothelial cells (including non-perfused vessels), enabling distinction between total vs. perfused networks. 1.1 Transcardial perfusion with 10 mL ice-cold PBS followed by 20 mL 4% PFA in PBS. 14.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 647, PSD-95 + Alexa Fluor 568, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-organic solvent clearing method that excels at preserving fine subcellular structures—including dendritic spines and synaptic puncta—while providing excellent transparency for 1–2 mm thick brain tissue blocks. It is highly compatible with immunolabeling of endogenous proteins and preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes effectively. The chosen markers target key excitatory postsynaptic scaffold proteins: Homer1 (postsynaptic density in CA1 dendritic spines), PSD-95 (core excitatory postsynaptic scaffold), and MAP2 (dendritic shaft marker to delineate dendritic arborization). This combination enables precise 3D quantification of synapse density, size, clustering, and laminar distribution within CA1 strata (stratum pyramidale vs. stratum radiatum).

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in CUBIC-A (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS): anti-Homer1 (1:200), anti-PSD-95 (1:200), anti-MAP2 (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Homer1/2/3 primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary, PSD-95 (DLG4) primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 594 secondary, MAP2 primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 647 secondary, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence exceptionally well—critical for multiplexed detection of synaptic proteins like Homer and PSD-95. It efficiently clears 1–2 mm tissue blocks within days without harsh organic solvents that quench fluorophores. The inclusion of MAP2 as a dendritic marker enables precise layer-specific analysis in CA1 (stratum pyramidale, radiatum, lacunosum-moleculare), while DAPI provides nuclear landmarks for laminar registration. CUBIC’s compatibility with standard antibody labeling and low tissue distortion makes it ideal for quantitative puncta analysis and spatial co-localization studies.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Fixation  
1.1 Post-fixation of dissected mouse hippocampal block (~1–2 mm thick) in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation in blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: anti-Homer1/2/3 (e.g., Synaptic Systems #160 011, 1:200), anti-PSD-95 (e.g., NeuroMab K28/43, 1:200), anti-MAP2 (e.g., Millipore AB5622, 1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day with 6 buffer changes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit (1:500), Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-mouse (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-chicken or appropriate host (1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day with 6 buffer changes)  
2.6 Counterstain with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 2 changes)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) NaCl in H₂O; RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
4.2 Store long-term in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark if not imaged immediately.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 month)

**Chosen Labeling:** [PSD95 + Alexa Fluor 488, Homer1 + Alexa Fluor 594, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, especially for thick (1–2 mm) fixed brain slices. The chosen markers target key excitatory postsynaptic scaffolds (PSD95 and Homer1) and the dendritic cytoskeleton (MAP2), enabling precise spatial mapping of synapses along dendrites while distinguishing true puncta from background. CUBIC’s gentle delipidation avoids over-shrinkage or loss of fine spine morphology, unlike harsh organic solvent methods (e.g., iDISCO+), which can quench Alexa Fluor signals and distort delicate dendritic arbors.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation (Assume 4% PFA-fixed mouse brain section containing hippocampal CA1, 1–2 mm thick)  
1.1 Wash in PBS (0.01 M phosphate-buffered saline, pH 7.4) to remove residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) for permeabilization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Labeling  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in CUBIC-A (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS): anti-PSD95 (1:200), anti-Homer1 (1:200), anti-MAP2 (1:300). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with CUBIC-A (without antibodies) to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 24 hours, gentle shaking)  

5 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
5.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-mouse/rabbit IgG, 1:300), Alexa Fluor 594 (1:300), and Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) in CUBIC-A. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Wash with CUBIC-A to remove unbound secondary antibodies. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 × 24 hours, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

7 Optical Clearing  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS) for initial clearing. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

8.2 Store at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ for long-term preservation (protected from light). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP, tdTomato, ELKS/CAST/ERC homolog + Alexa Fluor 488, Homer1 (implied by functional excitatory PSD distinction via ELKS vs. Homer; but restricted to given markers → use **ELKS/CAST/ERC homolog** and **Synapsin** as proxy for distinct PSD subtypes; labeled with **Alexa Fluor 488** and **Alexa Fluor 594**, respectively]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.49) clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP, tdTomato) and immunofluorescence signal with minimal tissue deformation—critical for accurate dendritic spine and synaptic puncta quantification in 1–2 mm thick CA1 blocks. It avoids organic solvents that quench GFP or cause shrinkage (unlike iDISCO+/uDISCO). CUBIC’s gentle delipidation and RI matching maintain fine neuropil architecture and synaptic protein epitopes. Alexa Fluor dyes are compatible with CUBIC and provide bright, photostable labeling for high-resolution imaging of synaptic scaffolds. ELKS/CAST/ERC homolog marks presynaptic active zones adjacent to PSDs, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicles; together they enable spatial discrimination of functionally distinct excitatory synapses when co-registered with postsynaptic dendrites (GFP/tdTomato-labeled neurons). All chosen fluorophores and markers are within the allowed lists.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation (Assume 4% PFA-fixed mouse brain section containing CA1, 1–2 mm thick block dissected in PBS)  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)  

2 Immunolabeling (Perform before clearing to preserve epitopes)  
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in Blocking Buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-ELKS/CAST/ERC homolog (1:200) and anti-Synapsin (1:300) in Antibody Dilution Buffer (5% NGS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 4 changes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse (1:500) in Antibody Dilution Buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 4 changes)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 3 changes)

4.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

5.1 Mount tissue in glass-bottom dish filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 488, Cx43 (Connexin 43) + Alexa Fluor 594, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method ideal for whole mouse hearts (~15–20 mm), offering excellent transparency while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence over weeks. It minimally distorts tissue architecture, crucial for maintaining myocardial fiber orientation. The selected markers target key components of the cardiac conduction system: Hcn4 labels the sinoatrial (SA) and atrioventricular (AV) nodes, Cx40 marks the His-Purkinje system (including bundle branches and Purkinje fibers), and Cx43 is enriched in working myocardium but excluded from nodal tissue—enabling precise delineation of conduction pathways. Phalloidin-AF647 provides F-actin–based myofiber orientation as a structural reference without interfering with conduction-specific signals. CUBIC’s compatibility with multi-day antibody penetration and RI matching to ~1.49 enables high-resolution light-sheet imaging of the entire intact heart.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) to remove residual fixative.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in blocking solution: anti-Hcn4 (1:200), anti-Cx40 (1:200), anti-Cx43 (1:200).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

3 Wash after Primary Antibody  
3.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Repeat PBST wash three times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

4 Secondary Antibody + Phalloidin Staining  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 594 anti-mouse, both 1:500) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

5 Wash after Secondary Antibody  
5.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Repeat PBST wash three times, each with fresh solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

6 CUBIC-L Delipidation and Clearing  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

7 Wash after CUBIC-L  
7.1 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Repeat PBS wash twice.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

8 CUBIC-R+ Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) NaCl in ddH₂O; RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  
8.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+ and incubate until full transparency is achieved (typically additional 2–4 days).(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 days)  

9 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer cleared heart into fresh CUBIC-R+ in a glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched cuvette.(Temperature: 4 ℃, long-term storage in dark)  
9.2 Equilibrate sample at RT for 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 / Hcn4 + Alexa Fluor 488, Cx43 (Connexin 43) + Alexa Fluor 594, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is ideal for whole mouse hearts (~15–20 mm) due to its high clearing efficiency in lipid-rich, dense tissues while preserving endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence. It is aqueous-based, minimizing tissue shrinkage and maintaining 3D architecture critical for analyzing spatial relationships between conduction system components and myocardial fiber orientation. Cx40/Hcn4 reliably labels the sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN)/His bundle regions, while Cx43 marks working myocardium and proximal Purkinje network; combined, they enable delineation of nodal vs. Purkinje vs. ventricular conduction territories. Phalloidin-AF647 provides high-fidelity F-actin labeling of cardiomyocyte sarcomeres to infer myofiber orientation as a structural scaffold. CUBIC’s compatibility with multi-color immunolabeling and RI matching to ~1.49 enables high-resolution light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Cx40 / Hcn4 (1:200) and anti-Cx43 (1:200) diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)

4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times with fresh CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)

6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)

7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)

8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

9.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 4 ℃, storage until imaging; image within 2 weeks)

1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HCN4 + Alexa Fluor 488, Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 594, cTnT + Alexa Fluor 647 (optional for fiber orientation), DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well, minimizes tissue deformation in soft organs like the heart, and effectively reduces lipofuscin-like autofluorescence through its amino alcohol-based reagents. It is compatible with multi-color immunolabeling of large tissues (~15–20 mm) without requiring harsh dehydration or organic solvents that quench fluorophores or distort fine structures like Purkinje fibers. The inclusion of cTnT (cardiac Troponin T) labeling with a far-red dye allows visualization of myocardial fiber architecture to contextualize conduction system pathways, while DAPI provides nuclear counterstain without interfering with green/red channels. CUBIC’s delipidation and decolorization steps significantly suppress myocardial background autofluorescence, which was a key issue in the prior DBE-based protocol.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (Perform after PFA fixation and post-fixation; skip methanol dehydration)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-HCN4 (1:200), anti-Cntn2 (1:200), optional anti-cTnT (1:300), in CUBIC-A solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
1.3 Wash with CUBIC-A: 3 changes over 2 days (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-rabbit (1:300), Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-mouse (1:300), optional Alexa Fluor 647 donkey anti-goat (1:300), plus 1 µg/mL DAPI, in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with CUBIC-A: 3 changes over 2 days (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours per wash)  

2 Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC-L)  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent: 25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

3 Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent: 50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 0.5% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate), in ddH₂O (RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  
3.2 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ for final equilibration (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Store cleared heart in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging  
4.2 Mount in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (no additional RI matching required)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and protein epitopes exceptionally well, making it ideal for immunolabeling of delicate neural structures in thick tissues like the intact mouse colon. It effectively clears lipid-rich tissues while maintaining layered architecture (e.g., mucosa, submucosa, muscularis externa), which is critical for distinguishing submucosal (SMP) and myenteric (MP) plexuses. HuC/D specifically labels neuronal nuclei and cytoplasm in the ENS, enabling clear identification of ganglia; PGP9.5 (ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1) is a pan-neuronal marker that robustly labels all ENS fibers and varicosities, revealing interganglionic connectivity. Phalloidin highlights F-actin in smooth muscle layers, providing structural context for plexus localization. DAPI counterstains nuclei to aid layer segmentation. CUBIC’s high refractive index matching (~1.49) is compatible with light-sheet and confocal microscopy, and its scalability suits 6–8 cm colon samples.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-HuC/D (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:400) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody + Phalloidin + DAPI Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 647 anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 568 (1:200), DAPI (1:1000) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

6 Post-Staining Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) N-butanediol, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
7.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, replace solution every 2–3 days)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
8.1 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Transfer sample into imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.49). Store at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ with 0.1% sodium azide for long-term preservation if not imaged immediately.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 594, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index (RI ≈ 1.49) clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well over long incubation periods—critical for thick, autofluorescence-prone tissues like the colon. It effectively clears lipid-rich muscular layers while maintaining structural integrity of mucosal folds and neural networks. The combination of HuC/D (pan-neuronal nuclear marker) and PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal cytoplasmic/axonal marker) provides complementary labeling of ENS neuronal somata and fibers across both myenteric and submucosal plexuses. Phalloidin-AF647 robustly labels F-actin in smooth muscle layers (circular/longitudinal) and epithelial actin belts, enabling precise layer segmentation. DAPI counterstains nuclei for tissue context. CUBIC’s compatibility with multi-day antibody penetration makes it ideal for 6–8 cm tubular organs requiring uniform labeling throughout.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B reagent (blocking buffer: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in CUBIC-B: anti-HuC/D (1:500), anti-PGP9.5 (1:400) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat 4.1 two more times with fresh CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody + Phalloidin + DAPI Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 donkey anti-mouse IgG 1:500, Alexa Fluor 594 donkey anti-rabbit IgG 1:500), Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200), and DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-Staining Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC-R+  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in ddH₂O; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
7.2 Replace with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
8.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in a light-protected imaging chamber (e.g., glass-bottom dish or capillary) (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
8.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R+ with 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [HuC/D + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling in large, intact tissues like the full-length mouse colon. It enables deep antibody penetration without harsh organic solvents that could damage delicate ENS structures or cause delamination of mucosal/muscular layers. HuC/D specifically labels neuronal nuclei/cytoplasm in enteric ganglia (ideal for identifying myenteric and submucosal neuron somata), while PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) robustly labels all neural processes throughout the ENS network. Dual-color labeling allows clear distinction between ganglia (HuC/D+) and dense fiber tracts (PGP9.5+), enabling topological analysis. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for layer identification. CUBIC’s strong delipidation and background-reducing properties effectively suppress autofluorescence from smooth muscle, resolving the previously reported high myenteric background that obscured plexus discrimination.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 15 vol% Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 10 vol% glycerol, 0.5 wt/vol casein in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Incubation  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-HuC/D (1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:400) diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

3 Washing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Repeat step 3.1 two additional times, changing solution every 24 hours (Total washing time: 72 hours)  

4 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

5 Post-Labeling Wash  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Repeat step 5.1 two additional times (Total washing time: 72 hours, protected from light)  

6 Tissue Clearing (Delipidation & Refractive Index Matching)  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (50 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 10 vol% glycerol in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50 vol% sucrose, 25 vol% urea, 10 vol% glycerol, 0.1 wt/vol sodium azide in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ and store at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging (stable for ≥4 weeks)  
7.2 Mount intact colon in a custom chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring minimal compression to preserve tubular architecture

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence exceptionally well across large tissues like whole mouse kidneys (~1 cm scale). It effectively homogenizes transparency between lipid-rich cortex and less-lipidic medulla, overcoming the皮髓透明不均 issue. The chosen labeling targets the slit diaphragm directly: Nephrin and Podocin are core structural components of the foot process slit diaphragm; Lectin labels glomerular endothelia to define capillary loops without replacing slit diaphragm signal; DAPI provides nuclear context for glomerular identification. CUBIC’s compatibility with multi-color immunolabeling and low tissue distortion enables accurate 3D quantification of glomerular number, volume, distribution, and slit diaphragm integrity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration (Optional pre-clearing wash)  
1.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for washing fixed kidney.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling (Perform before delipidation to preserve epitopes)  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Nephrin (1:200), anti-Podocin (1:200), anti-Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, 8 hours per change)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–donkey anti-rabbit, Alexa Fluor 594–donkey anti-goat, Alexa Fluor 647–streptavidin (if biotinylated lectin used), all at 1:500 in blocking solution + DAPI (1 µg/mL).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Washing with PBST (3 changes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total, 8 hours per change)  

3 Delipidation and Clearing (CUBIC-L)  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent: 25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2 days)  

4 Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent: 50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol (TDE), 0.1% (wt/vol) antifade (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in ddH₂O, RI ≈ 1.49.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking; replace once after 24 hours)  

5 Final Equilibration and Storage  
5.1 Transfer sample to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging-compatible glass vial.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ≥12 hours before imaging; store at 4 ℃ long-term)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 594]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling of large, fixed tissues like whole mouse kidneys (~1 cm scale). It enables deep, uniform antibody penetration without delipidation-induced epitope loss—critical for preserving the delicate slit diaphragm proteins Nephrin and Podocin. Alexa Fluor 488 and 594 offer bright, photostable signals with minimal spectral crosstalk, ideal for quantitative colocalization analysis in 3D. CUBIC’s RI matching (~1.49) is compatible with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives, and its gentle protocol maintains kidney architecture for accurate glomerular morphometry.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-40), 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) PVP-40, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Incubation  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) rabbit monoclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) goat polyclonal antibody (1:100) diluted in CUBIC-B + 5% donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (10% (wt/vol) PVP-40, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat step 4.1 two more times, changing solution daily (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

5 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (1:400) in CUBIC-B + 5% donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, protected from light)  

6 Post-labeling Washes  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-W1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 two more times (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

7 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) PVP-40 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) PVP-40, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Sample Mounting and Storage  
9.1 Transfer kidney into a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ and seal with coverslip using vacuum grease (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at 4 ℃ in dark for up to 2 weeks)
