**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (IB4)-Alexa Fluor 647, Nephrin-Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin-Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method ideal for whole mouse organs up to ~1 cm in size, offering excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence—critical for multi-color labeling of delicate structures like the slit diaphragm. It enables deep penetration of antibodies into intact kidneys without delipidation-induced epitope loss, which is essential for reliable detection of Nephrin and Podocin. Lectin/IB4 conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 labels glomerular endothelial lumens to delineate capillary loops, while DAPI provides nuclear context for cortical/medullary zonation. CUBIC’s RI (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet and confocal objectives, enabling high-resolution 3D mapping of glomeruli across kidney compartments.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Rehydration (if stored in methanol or ethanol post-fixation)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P (25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-40), 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with CUBIC-B (10% (wt/vol) PVP-40, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining (optional if directly using fluorescent conjugates; skip if using pre-conjugated antibodies)  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (1:200) and anti-Podocin (1:200) in CUBIC-B + 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 3 buffer changes)

4.1 Incubation with IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (10 µg/mL), DAPI (5 µg/mL), and if primary used, secondary antibodies (e.g., Alexa Fluor 488/555, 1:500) in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking)  
4.2 Wash with CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

5 CUBIC Clearing (Delipidation and Refractive Index Matching)  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking; replace solution every 2–3 days)

6.1 Transfer tissue to glass vial filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage at 4 ℃ in dark)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is ideal for lipid-rich, heterogeneous tissues like mouse kidney due to its strong delipidation and decolorization capacity while preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration. The original CUBIC-L/RA protocol was insufficient in duration and lacked adequate washing and permeabilization steps, leading to poor髓质 clearing and high background. Extending incubation times, adding a pre-clearing permeabilization step with Triton X-100, and incorporating a nuclear counterstain-compatible lectin (to label glomerular endothelia and enhance glomerular segmentation) significantly improves uniform transparency and signal-to-noise. Nephrin and Podocin are core slit diaphragm proteins; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes enables precise 3D reconstruction of filtration barrier integrity. Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum) binds glomerular endothelial glycocalyx, aiding glomerular identification without interfering with podocyte markers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Pre-Clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat ×3 with fresh solution)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Nephrin (1:200), anti-Podocin (1:200), and biotinylated Lectin (1:100) diluted in CUBIC-A (containing 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% (wt/vol) NaN₃) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

3 Post-Primary Wash  
3.1 Wash with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, repeat ×3)  

4 Secondary Antibody & Lectin Detection  
4.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rabbit IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-goat IgG (1:400), and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

5 Post-Secondary Wash  
5.1 Wash with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, repeat ×3)  

6 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC-L  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

7 Wash Prior to RI Matching  
7.1 Wash with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeat ×2)  

8 Refractive Index Matching with CUBIC-R+  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 30% (vol/vol) nicotinamide in H₂O; RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

9 Final Equilibration and Storage  
9.1 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging-compatible glass vial (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ≥12 hours before imaging; store at 4 ℃ long-term)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing two distinct retinal ganglion cell (RGC) projection pathways from retina through LGN to V1 using lipophilic carbocyanine dyes DiI and DiD, which stably incorporate into neuronal membranes and are compatible with methanol-based clearing protocols. iDISCO+ is optimal because: (1) it preserves lipophilic dye fluorescence far better than aqueous or high-temperature methods; (2) its delipidation step enhances tissue transparency while maintaining axonal morphology; (3) it is validated for whole-mount neural circuit tracing in mouse visual system structures of the given sizes (≤5 mm); and (4) it achieves high refractive index matching (~1.56) suitable for light-sheet imaging without distorting retinal lamination when dehydration is carefully controlled.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation / Bleaching (optional but recommended for endogenous fluorescence suppression)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (to prepare for optional post-fixation if needed; skip if samples already well-fixed)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Post-fixation (only if original fixation was suboptimal; otherwise skip)  
4.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Dehydration (repeat prior to clearing)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Dichloromethane (DCM) treatment  
6.1 Incubation with 100% dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)  

*Note: DiI and DiD labeling must be performed **prior to fixation or immediately after perfusion**, by pressure-injecting or crystal-embedding the dyes into specific retinal regions (e.g., nasal vs. temporal retina) and allowing diffusion for 1–2 weeks at 4 ℃ in 4% PFA before initiating this protocol. No additional antibody or nuclear counterstain is required per problem constraints.*

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires tracing distinct retinal projections using lipophilic carbocyanine dyes (DiI and DiD), which stably incorporate into neuronal membranes and are ideal for long-range axonal tracing. iDISCO+ is a methanol- and dichloromethane (DCM)-based organic solvent clearing method that preserves the fluorescence of these lipophilic dyes far better than aqueous or hydrogel-based methods. It efficiently clears lipid-rich neural tissues like retina, LGN, and V1 while maintaining fine axonal morphology and enabling high-resolution 3D imaging in light-sheet microscopy. Nuclear counterstains (e.g., DAPI) may be included as optional auxiliary signals for anatomical registration but are not primary tracers.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching (optional if endogenous pigments interfere)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (only if DiI/DiD labeling was performed post-fixation but pre-clearing; skip if dyes were injected in vivo and tissue is already fixed)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Lipophilic Tracer Labeling (if not already labeled in vivo; otherwise skip to Step 5)  
4.1 Microinjection or crystal placement of DiI (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindocarbocyanine perchlorate) and DiD (1,1'-dioctadecyl-3,3,3',3'-tetramethylindodicarbocyanine perchlorate) into distinct retinal regions (e.g., nasal vs. temporal retina) under stereomicroscope, followed by incubation in 4% PFA at 4 ℃ for 7–14 days to allow anterograde transport.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7–14 days)  

5 Dehydration (post-labeling, if labeling was done ex vivo)  
5.1 Repeat steps 1.1–1.6 exactly as above.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  

6 Dichloromethane (DCM) Treatment  
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (fresh batch).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)  

8 Optional Nuclear Counterstaining (for anatomical reference only)  
8.1 Prior to Step 1, if needed: incubate fixed tissue in 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS for 24 hours at 4 ℃ before dehydration.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours) — Note: DAPI signal may partially quench in iDISCO+; use only if essential for registration.

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is a recently developed, retina-optimized clearing method that preserves delicate laminar architecture of the neural retina while enabling deep imaging of lipophilic tracers like DiI/DiD. It uses a gentle, non-denaturing aqueous-based protocol with low detergent concentration, minimizing delamination and fluorescence quenching—critical for maintaining retinal layer integrity and long-range axonal signal from pre-labeled DiI/DiD. TO-PRO-3 is selected as a nuclear counterstain compatible with EyeCi and spectrally distinct from DiI (Ex/Em ~549/565 nm) and DiD (Ex/Em ~644/665 nm); it provides cytoarchitectural context in LGN and V1 without interfering with lipid dye signals or requiring antibody penetration.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration (if samples stored in methanol or dehydrated)  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 30 minutes)  

2 Post-fixation Stabilization (optional but recommended for DiI/DiD retention)  
2.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS (freshly diluted from 16% stock) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Nuclear Counterstaining with TO-PRO-3  
3.1 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 iodide (1:1000 dilution in PBST; final concentration ~1 µM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour, protected from light)  

4 EyeCi Clearing Solution Preparation (prepare fresh before use)  
4.1 Mix EyeCi-A: 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water (RI ≈ 1.38)  
4.2 Mix EyeCi-B: 25% (wt/vol) NMN, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (vol/vol) glycerol in distilled water (RI ≈ 1.45)  

5 Primary Clearing with EyeCi-A  
5.1 Incubation with EyeCi-A solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours, gentle shaking)  

6 Secondary Clearing with EyeCi-B  
6.1 Incubation with EyeCi-B solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, gentle shaking)  

7 Refractive Index Matching  
7.1 Transfer tissue to RIMS (Refractive Index Matching Solution): 88% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep™) in PBS, adjusted to RI = 1.45 with distilled water (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Optional: Replace with fresh RIMS for final imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

8 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Mount cleared retina, LGN, and V1 separately in glass-bottom dishes or capillaries filled with RIMS (RI = 1.45) (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)  
8.2 Protect samples from light during storage and imaging to preserve DiI/DiD fluorescence.

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is specifically optimized for retinal tissue, preserving laminar architecture and minimizing shrinkage—addressing the core issue of retinal wrinkling and layer disruption observed with other methods. It is compatible with lipophilic carbocyanine dyes (DiI/DiD), which are already used in the experiment, and effectively clears small neural tissues like LGN and V1 with low morphological distortion. The protocol avoids harsh organic solvents that extract or quench DiI/DiD signals and maintains low autofluorescence, enabling high-contrast 3D imaging of dual-color projection mapping across the visual pathway.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Stabilization  
2.1 Incubation with EyeCi-Delipidation Solution (5% (wt/vol) N-Lauroylsarcosine sodium salt in 100% methanol).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with fresh EyeCi-Delipidation Solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with EyeCi-RI Matching Solution (50% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh EyeCi-RI Matching Solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer samples to glass vials filled with fresh EyeCi-RI Matching Solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 2 weeks for optimal DiI/DiD signal)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues such as bone-encased cochleae, enabling efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving fine F-actin structures like stereocilia bundles. It maintains endogenous fluorescence and is compatible with antibody penetration in dense mineralized tissue. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in hair cell stereocilia with high specificity; Myosin VIIa is a well-established hair cell-specific marker that distinguishes inner and outer hair cells across cochlear turns; DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining for spatial reference. This combination allows 3D quantification of hair cell number, integrity, and stereocilia morphology throughout the intact spiral structure.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4) in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with daily solution change)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated 3 times)  

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (1:200 in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, repeated 4 times over 2 days)  

6 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin/DAPI Co-staining  
6.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated secondary antibody (1:300), Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100), and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, repeated 3 times over 1.5 days)  

8 Dehydration  
8.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated twice)  

9 Delipidation  
9.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeated twice)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI-matching solution (BABB-based: 1:2 (vol/vol) benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
10.2 Transfer to fresh BABB for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or capillary filled with BABB, sealed with nail polish to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa primary antibody + Alexa Fluor 568 secondary, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for hard tissues containing bone or cartilage—such as the intact mouse cochlea—and effectively decalcifies while preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration. It maintains F-actin integrity for Phalloidin labeling and supports robust immunostaining of intracellular proteins like Myosin VIIa, a well-established hair cell-specific marker in the inner ear. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles without requiring antibodies, fulfilling the requirement to avoid unnecessary substitution. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular context. The method achieves high transparency with refractive index (RI ≈ 1.52) compatible with high-NA oil or silicone immersion objectives for confocal or light-sheet imaging of all cochlear turns.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Post-fixation and Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for re-fixation if not freshly fixed.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with BoneClear Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, pH 7.4, in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with daily solution change)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with BoneClear Permeabilization Solution (5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with BoneClear Blocking Buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Immunolabeling and Phalloidin Staining  
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody against Myosin VIIa (1:200 dilution in blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit (or appropriate host) secondary antibody (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in blocking buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  
3.4 Wash with PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 × 2 hours, protected from light)  

4 Dehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 1 hour)  

5 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution A (1:1 mixture of benzyl alcohol and benzyl benzoate, BABB).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution B (pure BABB).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
6.2 Mount in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for confocal or light-sheet microscopy using silicone oil (RI = 1.40) or BABB-matched immersion objective (RI = 1.56).

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 488, Phalloidin + Alexa Fluor 568, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for small, dense, bone-containing tissues like the mouse cochlea because it combines effective delipidation and decalcification steps with excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence. It enables deep penetration of antibodies into mineralized tissue after EDTA decalcification and provides high transparency with refractive index matching in dichloromethane (DCM) and dibenzyl ether (DBE), compatible with light-sheet and confocal imaging. The labeling strategy targets: (1) Myosin VIIa to specifically identify inner and outer hair cells; (2) Phalloidin to label F-actin–rich stereocilia bundles at the apical surface; and (3) β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker that robustly labels cochlear nerve fibers, including their terminal arborizations beneath hair cells—enabling precise 3D mapping of neural innervation relative to hair cell morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 7.4, in PBS) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Bleaching (optional, if autofluorescence is high)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Staining  
6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:500), anti-β-III Tubulin/TUJ1 (1:500) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Repeat wash step 7.1 two more times, changing solution daily. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

8 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
8.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit (1:500, for Myosin VIIa), Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse (1:500, for TUJ1), and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated Phalloidin (1:100) in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide + 5% (vol/vol) donkey serum. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)  

9 Post-staining Wash  
9.1 Incubation with PBST + 5% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
9.2 Repeat wash step 9.1 two more times, changing solution daily. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours each)  

10 Dehydration (post-staining)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM):methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Repeat step 11.2 once. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Transfer sample to fresh DBE in glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched RI cuvette. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Mount cleared cochlea in DBE-filled imaging chamber with coverslip sealed using VALAP or nail polish. Protect from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage up to 1 week at RT in dark)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Myosin VIIa + Alexa Fluor 488 (or equivalent Alexa Fluor conjugate), Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568/647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS is specifically optimized for hard tissues containing bone and cartilage—such as the intact mouse cochlea—and achieves high transparency while preserving endogenous fluorescence and immunolabeling. It combines decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching in a single workflow compatible with F-actin (Phalloidin) and protein (Myosin VIIa) labeling. Myosin VIIa is a well-established hair cell identity marker; Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles with high specificity; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain without interfering with far-red channels. This combination enables robust 3D visualization of inner/outer hair cell patterning, stereocilia integrity, and regional pathology across cochlear turns with minimal tissue distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification & Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-A1 (20% (wt/vol) EDTA, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Wash with PBT (0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours × 3 changes)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-Myosin VIIa (1:200 in blocking solution) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.4 Wash with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 3 changes)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:400) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 568 (1:100) + DAPI (1 µg/mL) in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Wash with PBT (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour × 2 changes)  

4 Delipidation & Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with PEGASOS-B (8% (wt/vol) benzyl alcohol, 8% (wt/vol) benzyl benzoate, 33% (wt/vol) PEG 400, 51% (wt/vol) DMSO) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP + Alexa Fluor 488, S100β + Alexa Fluor 594, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, lipid-rich neural tissues like the rat spinal cord (~40 mm long), offering deep clearing with excellent preservation of protein epitopes and endogenous/exogenous fluorescence. It enables robust immunolabeling in thick samples without hydrogel embedding, which is critical for detecting subtle differences in astrocyte reactivity (via GFAP upregulation and S100β co-expression) and assessing axonal penetration through glial scars (via TUJ1). The organic solvent-based RI matching (DBE, RI ≈ 1.56) provides high transparency and compatibility with light-sheet microscopy. GFAP marks all astrocytes but is strongly upregulated in reactive states; S100β complements this by labeling both resting and reactive astrocytes, allowing discrimination of activation levels. TUJ1 labels regenerating or spared axons to evaluate scar barrier function.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash in PBS (3 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Store in PBS with 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide at 4 ℃ until processing (max 1 week)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Bleaching (optional for endogenous fluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with blocking solution: PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Primary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in antibody dilution buffer (PBST + 10% DMSO + 6% donkey serum): anti-GFAP (1:500), anti-S100β (1:500), anti-β-III Tubulin/TUJ1 (1:500) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, gentle shaking)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Wash with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (4 changes over 2 days) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

8 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
8.1 Incubation with species-specific secondary antibodies conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (anti-rabbit/mouse, 1:500), Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500), and Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light, gentle shaking)  

9 Wash  
9.1 Wash with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO (4 changes over 2 days) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours per wash)  
9.2 Final wash with PBST (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  

10 Dehydration (post-immunolabeling)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (2 changes) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Transfer to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial (Temperature: RT, store protected from light)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Mount cleared spinal cord segment vertically in a glass capillary or chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI = 1.56)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFAP + Alexa Fluor 647, β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for large, lipid-rich neural tissues like the intact rat spinal cord (~40 mm long). It provides deep, uniform clearing with excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, critical for resolving fine axonal processes within dense glial scars. The organic solvent–based protocol efficiently removes lipids while maintaining structural integrity over centimeter-scale samples. GFAP robustly labels reactive astrocytic scar borders, while β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) specifically marks neuronal axons—including regenerating fibers—enabling precise 3D spatial analysis of axon–scar interactions. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 offer high photostability and minimal spectral crosstalk in light-sheet microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) after dissection. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash in PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.3 Store in PBS with 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide at 4 ℃ until processing. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 week)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

3 Bleaching (optional for autofluorescence reduction)  
3.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Rehydration  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Permeabilization and Blocking  
5.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with blocking solution (6% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

6.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-GFAP (1:500) and anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (3% (vol/vol) donkey serum, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.3 M glycine in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

7 Washes After Primary Antibody  
7.1 Wash with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) six times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

8 Secondary Antibody Labeling  
8.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)  

9 Washes After Secondary Antibody  
9.1 Wash with wash buffer (10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) six times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours per wash)  

10 Dehydration (Post-Labeling)  
10.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.5 Incubation with 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Delipidation  
11.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Repeat incubation with fresh DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

12 Refractive Index Matching  
12.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
12.2 Transfer to fresh DBE in imaging-compatible glass vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes before imaging)  

13 Imaging Preparation  
13.1 Mount cleared spinal cord vertically or horizontally in a glass capillary or chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM). Ensure no air bubbles. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or store at RT in dark for ≤1 week)

**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of lipid-rich, pigmented tissues like the mouse heart. Its methanol-based dehydration and dichloromethane (DCM)-based delipidation effectively remove hemoglobin and myoglobin-derived red autofluorescence while preserving endogenous fluorescence and enabling deep antibody penetration. The method achieves high transparency in dense myocardium and supports multiplex immunolabeling with organic fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes), which are more photostable than fluorescent proteins in harsh organic solvents. ChAT specifically labels cholinergic intrinsic cardiac neurons/ganglia; TH marks noradrenergic sympathetic fibers; cTnT provides cardiomyocyte structural reference for anatomical registration; DAPI enables nuclear counterstaining without interfering with neural signals. **Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, ChAT + Alexa Fluor 594, cTnT + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is ideal for whole-organ clearing of fixed mouse hearts (~10 mm scale) due to its strong delipidation capacity, excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence (especially Alexa Fluor dyes), and compatibility with methanol-based dehydration that reduces tissue swelling. It enables deep penetration of antibodies in dense cardiac tissue and achieves high transparency with refractive index matching in dichloromethane (DCM) and dibenzyl ether (DBE), suitable for light-sheet imaging. The labeling strategy uses well-validated primary antibodies against TH (tyrosine hydroxylase, sympathetic marker) and ChAT (choline acetyltransferase, parasympathetic marker), combined with cTnT (cardiac troponin T) to delineate myocardial architecture and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining—enabling precise 3D mapping of neural innervation relative to cardiac structures.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃ (blocking buffer).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing rabbit anti-TH (1:200), goat anti-ChAT (1:100), and mouse anti-cTnT (1:200), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with blocking buffer containing donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 594 (1:200), and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-Secondary Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBT + 0.2% (wt/vol) NaN₃.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 five times, changing solution daily.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour before imaging)  

12 Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Mount cleared heart in glass-bottom dish or custom chamber filled with DBE, avoiding bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark)

CUBIC-R+ provides high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.49) compatible with light-sheet microscopy, with minimal tissue distortion. The inclusion of DAPI enables nuclear counterstaining for anatomical reference without spectral overlap. This protocol integrates full delipidation, decolorization, permeabilization, blocking, and extended antibody penetration tailored for dense cardiac tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decolorization & Delipidation (CUBIC-L)  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Wash with PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 buffer changes)  

3 Permeabilization & Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBST) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-ChAT (1:100) diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 14 days, with gentle shaking)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with PBST (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, with 6 buffer changes every 8 hours)

6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:400), plus DAPI (1:1000), all diluted in blocking solution (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647), CD31 (Alexa Fluor 488), LYVE-1 (Alexa Fluor 594)]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a rapid, aqueous-based clearing method compatible with endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, preserving protein epitopes well for immunolabeling—critical for distinguishing liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) markers (LYVE-1 and Stabilin-2/LYVE-1 surrogate) from pan-endothelial CD31. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* IB4) robustly labels perfused vasculature including sinusoids and portal vessels. Given the 1 mm thickness and 24-hour timeline, CUBIC’s fast delipidation and RI matching (<24 h total) are ideal. LYVE-1 specifically marks LSECs, while CD31 labels all endothelia (including portal triads and central veins); Lectin provides complementary vascular lumen contrast. Alexa Fluor dyes offer high photostability and compatibility with CUBIC’s high-pH environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with CUBIC-L (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.05% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) for permeabilization (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling and Lectin Staining  
2.1 Blocking in CUBIC-B (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-CD31 (1:200) and anti-LYVE-1 (1:100), plus biotinylated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin (10 µg/mL), all diluted in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-rat IgG (for CD31), Alexa Fluor 594 anti-hamster IgG (for LYVE-1), and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated streptavidin (for Lectin), all at 1:500 in CUBIC-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in H₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in H₂O; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Equilibration in CUBIC-R+ (RI = 1.52; 50% (wt/vol) iohexol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 10% (vol/vol) ethanol in H₂O) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Mount tissue in glass-bottom dish or chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for immediate confocal imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: proceed to imaging)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67 (MKI67) + Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA + Alexa Fluor 594, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling of nuclear and cell cycle proteins in small tissues like ~300 μm human intestinal organoids. It achieves high transparency within 1–2 days without harsh organic solvents that could disrupt delicate 3D architecture. Ki67 marks proliferating cells across all active phases of the cell cycle, while PCNA labels DNA replication foci during S-phase—providing complementary proliferation readouts. Hoechst serves as a nuclear counterstain to delineate epithelial nuclei without interfering with Alexa Fluor channels. CUBIC’s high refractive index (~1.49) matches well with standard light-sheet/confocal objectives.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Permeabilization and Blocking  
1.1 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC blocking solution (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Primary Antibody Staining  
2.1 Incubation with anti-Ki67 (1:200) and anti-PCNA (1:200) diluted in CUBIC antibody dilution buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3 Wash  
3.1 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  

4 Secondary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400), plus Hoechst (1:1000), all diluted in CUBIC antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Wash with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)  

6 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC Reagent 1  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R1 (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R1 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Refractive Index Matching with CUBIC Reagent 2  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R2 (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) 2,2′-thiodiethanol in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

8 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
8.1 Transfer organoids into glass-bottom imaging dish containing fresh CUBIC-R2 for immediate imaging or store at 4 ℃ in CUBIC-R2 (sealed, protected from light) for up to 1 week.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor 594, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence exceptionally well in thick tissue sections (~500 μm), making it ideal for high-resolution 3D imaging of delicate renal structures like the glomerular filtration barrier. It minimizes protein denaturation compared to organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+), which is critical for preserving conformational epitopes of Nephrin and Podocin. The chosen triple-labeling strategy targets: (1) Nephrin (slit diaphragm core protein), (2) Podocin (podocyte slit diaphragm scaffold), and (3) IB4 lectin (labels glomerular endothelial glycocalyx), collectively resolving all three layers of the filtration barrier. Alexa Fluor dyes offer high photostability and compatibility with CUBIC’s high-pH environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  
1.3 Store in PBS at 4 ℃ until processing (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ≤1 week)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation in CUBIC-P1 (10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (wt/vol) urea in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation in blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Incubation with anti-Nephrin (NPHS1) rabbit monoclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Podocin (NPHS2) mouse monoclonal antibody (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (5% NGS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

5 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500), Alexa Fluor 594–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated IB4 lectin (10 μg/mL) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-Staining Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

7 Optical Clearing with CUBIC Reagents  
7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
7.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Refractive Index Matching  
8.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) antifade reagent (e.g., n-propyl gallate) in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
9.1 Transfer tissue into a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for ≤1 week)

NeuN specifically labels mature neuronal nuclei, while MAP2 robustly stains neuronal somata and dendrites; pairing them with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes ensures clear dual-channel visualization of mature neuron morphology throughout the 2 mm depth. CUBIC’s high refractive index matching (RI ≈ 1.49) aligns well with light-sheet microscopy objectives.

1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Permeabilization and Blocking  
2.1 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 reagent (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) and chicken anti-MAP2 (1:1000) diluted in CUBIC-A (10% (wt/vol) polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Washing  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Repeat 4.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)

5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-chicken IgG Alexa Fluor 594 (1:500) diluted in CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  

6 Post-labeling Wash  
6.1 Incubation with CUBIC-A (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes, each 24 hours)

7.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in ddH₂O) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2–3 days)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA + Alexa Fluor 488, Collagen IV + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence well in thick (~2 mm) soft tissues like myocardium. It is compatible with antibody penetration and retains protein epitopes for robust immunostaining of cytoskeletal (α-SMA) and basement membrane (Collagen IV) structures. α-SMA labels both vascular smooth muscle cells and activated myofibroblasts in fibrotic regions; Collagen IV delineates vascular basement membranes to reconstruct coronary vasculature; DAPI provides nuclear context. CUBIC’s RI matching (~1.49) is ideal for light-sheet or confocal imaging of cleared cardiac tissue without delipidation-induced antigen loss seen in organic solvent methods.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Fixation and Storage  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS (pH 7.4) overnight at 4 ℃ after initial dissection. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12–16 hours)  
1.2 Wash thoroughly with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST) to remove residual PFA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in Blocking Buffer (10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding and enhance antibody penetration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-α-SMA (1:200) and rabbit anti-Collagen IV (1:200) diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer (5% NGS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Wash with PBST to remove unbound primary antibodies. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all in Antibody Dilution Buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking in the dark)  
2.5 Wash thoroughly with PBST to remove unbound fluorophores. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  

3 CUBIC Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) for delipidation and initial clearing. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.2 Wash with PBS to remove residual CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49) for refractive index matching. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 days with gentle shaking)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Final equilibration in fresh CUBIC-R+ to ensure homogeneity and optical clarity. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Mount tissue in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 1 week)

Lectin perfusion labels only functional, blood-perfused vascular lumens, while CD31 immunostaining reveals the full endothelial network—enabling dual visualization of structure and function. DAPI provides nuclear reference without interfering with alveolar architecture. iDISCO+’s organic solvent-based protocol minimizes tissue swelling, preserving delicate alveolar morphology better than aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC or ScaleS).

1 Perfusion and Fixation (assumed pre-step; included for completeness)

1.2 Post-fixation of dissected 1.5 mm lung block in 4% PFA.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.6 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
4.5 Incubation with 100% PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC) + Alexa Fluor 488, CD35 (CR1/2) + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling in small tissues like mouse lymph nodes (~3 mm). It enables deep, uniform antibody penetration while maintaining fine structural integrity of lymphoid architecture, including follicles and germinal centers. B220 (pan-B cell marker) delineates all B cell zones, while CD35 (complement receptor 1/2) specifically labels follicular dendritic cell networks within germinal centers—providing complementary structural definition of lymphoid follicles. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 offer high photostability, minimal spectral overlap, and excellent compatibility with CUBIC’s high-refractive-index matching solutions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

3 Immunolabeling  
3.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-B220 (rat IgG2b, 1:200) and anti-CD35 (clone 8C12, hamster IgG, 1:100) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-rat IgG–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-hamster IgG–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  
3.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 1 hour)  

4 CUBIC Clearing – Delipidation & Decolorization  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (10% (wt/vol) N-butanediol, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-L.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 CUBIC Clearing – Refractive Index Matching  
5.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) triethanolamine, 0.5% (wt/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water; RI ≈ 1.49).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 Incubation with fresh CUBIC-R+.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

6 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
6.1 Transfer tissue to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dish or capillary tube.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
6.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark if imaging delayed beyond 48 hours.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated) + Stabilin-2 (primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 488 secondary]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, high-refractive-index clearing method that preserves endogenous and immunolabeled fluorescence exceptionally well in large, lipid-rich organs like the adult mouse liver. It minimizes tissue deformation—critical for accurate vascular topology—and is compatible with both lectin perfusion labeling and antibody-based detection. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) robustly labels all vascular endothelia including liver sinusoids, while Stabilin-2 is a highly specific marker for liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs), ensuring complete coverage of the hepatic microvasculature without reliance on generic markers like CD31, which under-labels sinusoids. Alexa Fluor dyes are chosen for their photostability and compatibility with CUBIC’s high-pH environment.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Perfusion and Fixation  
1.1 Transcardial perfusion with 20 mL ice-cold PBS followed by 20 mL 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: ~10 min total perfusion)  
1.2 Excise whole liver and post-fix in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Lectin Vascular Labeling (performed before delipidation to ensure luminal access)  
2.1 Perfuse fixed liver via portal vein with 50 µg/mL Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour incubation with gentle rocking)  
2.2 Wash thoroughly with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Immunolabeling for Stabilin-2  
3.1 Incubate liver in blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-Stabilin-2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours, change buffer every 12 h)  
3.4 Incubate with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
3.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 12 hours)  

4 CUBIC Clearing  
4.1 Incubate in CUBIC-L (25% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 15% (wt/vol) sucrose, 10% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in H₂O).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking; replace solution every 2–3 days)  
4.2 Wash with CUBIC-R+ (50% (wt/vol) sucrose, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) Quadrol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in H₂O).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 × 6 hours)  
4.3 Incubate in CUBIC-R+ for refractive index matching.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking until transparent; replace once at day 3)  

5 Final RI Matching and Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Transfer cleared liver to fresh CUBIC-R+ in imaging-compatible glass-bottom dish or chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour equilibration before imaging)  
5.2 Store long-term in CUBIC-R+ at 4 ℃ in the dark if not imaged immediately.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2) + Alexa Fluor 594, IB4 + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based, non-organic solvent clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and is highly compatible with immunolabeling in thick tissues like the whole mouse kidney (~3–4 mm). It effectively clears lipid-rich renal tissue while maintaining fine ultrastructural integrity of glomeruli and vasculature. Nephrin and podocin are core slit diaphragm proteins whose co-localization directly reports on glomerular filtration barrier integrity. IB4 (Isolectin B4) robustly labels endothelial cells in murine kidney vasculature without requiring transgenic labeling, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular context. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/594/647 and DAPI) are well-preserved under CUBIC conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB), pH 7.4, to wash out residual fixative. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with CUBIC-P1 (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 15 vol% Triton X-100 in distilled water) for permeabilization and delipidation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution: CUBIC-B (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 10 vol% DMSO, 0.5 vol% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibodies diluted in CUBIC-B: anti-Nephrin (1:200), anti-Podocin (1:200). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle shaking)  
2.3 Washing with CUBIC-W (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 0.5 vol% Triton X-100 in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies and probes diluted in CUBIC-B: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 594-conjugated anti-goat IgG (1:400), Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated IB4 (10 µg/mL), DAPI (5 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Washing with CUBIC-W. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  

3 Optical Clearing  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 vol% Quadrol, 25 vol% urea, 10 vol% DMSO, 0.5 vol% Triton X-100 in distilled water) for initial refractive index (RI) matching. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% triethanolamine, 0.1 wt% Triton X-100, adjusted to RI = 1.49) for final clearing and RI homogenization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Equilibration in fresh CUBIC-R+ to ensure full transparency and RI stability. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Mount sample in a glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ for light-sheet microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 488, CD68+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized tissues such as mouse calvaria, enabling efficient decalcification and lipid removal while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody-based labeling. It achieves high transparency in ~1 mm thick bone with minimal distortion of immune cell morphology. The dual immunolabeling strategy targets B220 (pan-immune B-cell marker) and CD68 (myeloid/macrophage lineage), complemented by DAPI for nuclear counterstaining—ideal for resolving 3D distribution of both broad immune populations and myeloid subsets within the marrow cavity. BoneClear’s aqueous-based protocol is compatible with standard fluorescent dyes and antibodies, unlike organic solvent–based methods (e.g., iDISCO+) that often quench Alexa Fluor signals.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification & Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with BoneClear Decalcification Solution (0.5 M EDTA, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle agitation and solution refreshed every 2 days)  

2 Wash  
2.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated 3 times)  

3 Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with Blocking Buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

4 Primary Antibody Staining  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: rat anti-B220 (1:200) and rat anti-CD68 (1:200) diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, with gentle agitation)  

5 Wash  
5.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, repeated 4 times over 2 days)  

6 Secondary Antibody & Nuclear Staining  
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 594 (1:400), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days, protected from light)  

7 Wash  
7.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours, repeated 3 times over 1.5 days)  

8 Optical Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with BoneClear Clearing Solution C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with BoneClear RI Matching Solution (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 35% (wt/vol) urea in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

10 Storage & Imaging Preparation  
10.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with BoneClear RI Matching Solution and seal for light-sheet microscopy (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)

2.1 Incubation with fluorescently conjugated Lectin/IB4 (e.g., IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, 10 µg/mL) in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.2 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
2.3 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with PBST containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Primary antibody incubation: anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) and anti-Osterix (1:100) in PBST + 5% serum + 5% DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
2.6 Secondary antibody incubation: Alexa Fluor 488 anti-mouse (for Osteocalcin) and Alexa Fluor 555 anti-rabbit (for Osx), both at 1:500 in PBST + 5% serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 × 2 hours)  
2.8 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

Tomato lectin (Lycopersicon esculentum) binds to vascular endothelia and provides robust labeling of pulp vasculature without requiring transgenic models.
